title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addresses valedictory session of 31st CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam
subtitle:
Vice-President calls for translating investment commitments into tangible outcomes; lauds Andhra Pradesh’s development trajectory

Andhra Pradesh emerging as a major gateway for India’s global economic engagement: Vice-President

India aspires not merely to participate in the emerging global economic order but to play a leading role in shaping it: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 6:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today addressed the valedictory session of the 31st edition of the CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh.
The Vice-President appreciated the remarkable development achieved by Andhra Pradesh under the leadership of Chief Minister Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu.He noted that the State had attracted 714 investment projects worth over ₹22 lakh crore since June 2024, reflecting strong investor confidence and economic momentum.
He said that the State’s vision of Swarna Andhra 2047 was aligned with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. Investments in green energy, artificial intelligence, semiconductors, quantum technology, ports, aerospace and advanced manufacturing were positioning Andhra Pradesh as an emerging industrial and innovation hub.
Referring to the theme of this year’s Summit, ‘Navigating the New World Order – Trade, Technology and Trust’, the Vice-President observed that geopolitical uncertainties, technological disruptions, climate change and evolving supply chains were reshaping the global economy. However, every period of uncertainty also presented new opportunities, and nations demonstrating adaptability, innovation and trusted partnerships would be best placed to shape the future.
He expressed confidence that India, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, was moving firmly towards becoming a developed nation by 2047. Emphasising India’s growing economic strength, young and skilled workforce, vibrant entrepreneurial ecosystem and expanding manufacturing and services sectors, he said that India aspired not merely to participate in the emerging global economic order but to play a leading role in shaping it.
The Vice-President highlighted the transformative potential of artificial intelligence, semiconductors, quantum computing, biotechnology, advanced manufacturing and digital platforms. He stressed that Atmanirbhar Bharat should not be understood as turning inward, but as building domestic capabilities, enhancing competitiveness and integrating more deeply with global markets.
Calling for a collective national endeavour towards Viksit Bharat 2047, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan emphasised that the responsibility of building a developed India could not rest with the Government alone. It required the active participation of industry, academia, entrepreneurs, young people and international partners, in keeping with the Prime Minister’s call for Sabka Prayas.
Concluding his address, the Vice-President called upon stakeholders to move from dialogue to action, from opportunity to achievement, and from partnership to shared prosperity. He expressed appreciation to all participating countries, international delegates, industry leaders and institutions for their contribution to the Summit.
The Governor of Andhra Pradesh, Shri S. Abdul Nazeer; Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, Shri N Chandrababu Naidu;Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy, Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi; Union Minister for Civil Aviation, Shri Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu; Andhra Pradesh Ministers Shri Nara Lokesh and Shri T. G. Bharath; CII Director General Shri Chandrajit Banerjee; and CII President Designate Dr. Suchitra Ella, among other dignitaries, were present on the occasion.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium, India's first LED dome planetarium in Mysuru, Karnataka
subtitle:
The new COSMOS Planetarium in Mysuru brings the wonders of the universe closer to young minds: PM

There were many great astronomers in India like Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Bhaskaracharya, and Nilakantha Somayaji; Advanced instruments and technology like today were not available at that time; Despite this, they made great discoveries and performed difficult calculations: PM

Our government has opened up the space sector; This has created new avenues for private sector, providing Indian startups with the opportunity to showcase their potential: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 7:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated the COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium, India's first LED dome planetarium, in Mysuru, Karnataka. Addressing the gathering on the occasion, the Prime Minister extended his greetings in Kannada, and expressed his delight at returning to Mysuru to dedicate the COSMOS Planetarium to the nation just months after inaugurating the Viveka Smaraka. Pointing out that while the Viveka Smaraka inspires introspection and spiritual pursuit, the COSMOS Planetarium directs our gaze skyward to unravel the mysteries of the vast universe, he emphasized the profound cultural message conveyed by both landmarks. “This is an example of the fact that in India, the traditions of spirituality and science have always moved forward together,” remarked Shri Modi.
Recalling how ancient Indian ancestors minutely studied the skies, understood planetary and stellar movements, created calendars, and calculated solar and lunar eclipses, the Prime Minister highlighted the legacy of great Indian astronomers such as Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Bhaskaracharya, and Nilakantha Somayaji. “Advanced instruments and technology like today did not exist at that time; despite this, they made great discoveries and performed difficult calculations,” noted PM Modi.
Highlighting Mysuru's rich tradition of fostering knowledge institutions,including the establishment of the University of Mysore under Maharaja Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar and the Wadiyar royal family's pivotal role in laying the foundation of the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru to empower generations of scholars, the Prime Minister noted that Mysuru is adding a new chapter to India's scientific journey with the dedication of this state-of-the-art planetarium to the youth and citizens. Sharing that watching a show inside the LED dome was a wonderful experience in itself, he congratulated the nation on the milestone. “I felicitate the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, the University of Mysore, various departments of the government, and all the people associated with its construction,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Tracing the evolution of India's national motto from ‘Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan’ to Atal Bihari Vajpayee's addition of ‘Jai Vigyan’ and his own addition of ‘Jai Anusandhan’ guiding 21st-century India, the Prime Minister praised the enthusiastic participation of Indian youth when Mumbai hosted the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics last year and highlighted their stellar performance at this year's edition in Vietnam. “Five students from India went to Vietnam; out of them, four won gold medals and one won a silver medal, which is a matter of pride for the entire country,” observed PM Modi.
Spotlighting the record-breaking achievements of young Indian students who won gold or silver medals across Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, and Biology at this year's International Olympiads, the Prime Minister emphasized that young Indians achieve extraordinary milestones whenever they are provided with learning resources, technology, tools, and institutional support. “This COSMOS Planetarium is now also going to help immensely in giving shape to their dreams,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Emphasizing that no nation can afford to move slowly amid rapid global technological change, the Prime Minister detailed India's unprecedented pace over the past decade in astronomy, astrophysics, and space exploration through new telescopes and landmark ISRO missions, including becoming the first country to land near the Moon's South Pole with Chandrayaan-3 and launching India's first space solar observatory, Aditya-L1. “Last year itself, India became the fourth country in the world to demonstrate the capability of docking and undocking in space,” noted PM Modi.
Pointing out that an Indian astronaut recently traveled to the International Space Station and conducted novel experiments during this period, the Prime Minister highlighted the strategic value of the mission's findings. “The experience gained from this mission is also proving useful for our own human spaceflight program, Gaganyaan,” observed Shri Modi.
Highlighting the government's decision to open the space sector to private participation, which has enabled Indian startups and youth to showcase their capabilities by launching private rockets, placing satellites into orbit, and undertaking unprecedented space ventures, the Prime Minister stated that this reflects the scientific approach of New India. “Where new discoveries are being encouraged, new technology is being developed, and new opportunities are being created for our youth,” asserted PM Modi.
Underscoring that India has always been guided by the mantra of ‘Humanity First’ and dedicated its space program to human welfare, the Prime Minister cited the ISRO-developed satellite communication system for fishermen. “With the help of this system, for the boats fitted with receivers, officials can deliver timely alerts to them during a storm and can also track their safe return to the shore,” noted Shri Modi.
Detailing everyday applications of space technology such as the Real-Time Train Tracking System developed by Indian Railways and ISRO for checking live train locations and the use of satellite data alongside field inputs under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana to estimate crop yields and settle farm insurance claims, the Prime Minister highlighted the dual impact of India's space assets. “Today our satellites are touching the heights of space, and at the same time, they are being used to make the lives of people better on Earth,” observed PM Modi.
Emphasizing that the government's guiding philosophy of ‘Science for Society’ drives its sustained push for research and innovation across the country, the Prime Minister noted that over one crore students have already benefited from more than 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs nationwide. “In these labs, children are getting opportunities to work on their ideas, conduct new experiments, and innovate,” noted Shri Modi.
Stating that advancing research requires giving students and scholars access to the world's finest scientific literature, the Prime Minister highlighted the launch of ‘One Nation One Subscription’ to help domestic institutes access leading global journals alongside the creation of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation. “Through this, we are helping the maximum number of universities to conduct new research,” asserted PM Modi.
Recalling last year's launch of the one lakh crore rupee Research, Development, and Innovation Scheme to ensure sustained funding for domestic researchers, the Prime Minister highlighted the practical impact of the initiative. “This is helping in taking new technology out of the lab and reaching it to practical use,” observed Shri Modi.
Concluding his address by stating that planetariums and science centers play a vital role in sparking youth curiosity within India's burgeoning science and research ecosystem, the Prime Minister urged those associated with COSMOS to continuously invite school and college students from across the region and extended his best wishes for the journey ahead. “The children who come here to learn about the universe, it is possible that some of them may return here one day and tell us what new discoveries they have made about the universe, and this alone will be the biggest success of this COSMOS Planetarium,” remarked PM Modi.

title: English rendering of PM’s address at the inauguration of COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium in Mysuru, Karnataka
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
My Greetings to everyone!
Governor of Karnataka, Sudha Yadav Ji, Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar Ji, my Cabinet colleague, Nirmala Sitharaman Ji, Minister in the State Government, Basavaraj Rayareddy Ji, my colleague in Parliament, Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar Ji, all the scientists, researchers, teachers, other distinguished dignitaries, and my dear brothers and sisters of Mysuru.
First of all, I respectfully bow to Tai Chamundeshwari. I am very happy to be here in Mysuru once again. Just a few months ago, I had come among you for the inauguration of the Viveka Smaraka. And today, we have gathered here to dedicate the COSMOS Planetarium to the nation. Both these occasions convey a profound message about India's values and our culture. Viveka Smaraka inspires us to look within ourselves and seek spiritual knowledge. At COSMOS, on the other hand, our eyes are lifted towards the sky. We are inspired to explore this vast universe and understand its mysteries. This is an example of how the traditions of spirituality and science in India have always progressed side by side.
Friends,
Our ancestors used to study the sky very closely. They understood the movements of stars and planets, prepared calendars and calculated the timings of solar and lunar eclipses. India was home to many great astronomers such as Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Bhaskaracharya and Nilakantha Somayaji. The advanced instruments and technologies that are available today did not exist at that time. Despite this, they made great discoveries and carried out even the most difficult calculations.
Friends,
Mysuru has a tradition of establishing institutions that encourage the pursuit of knowledge. The University of Mysore was established during the reign of Maharaja Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar. The Wadiyar family also played an important role in laying the foundation of the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru. These institutions have provided generations of students and researchers with opportunities to advance. And today, when India is achieving one milestone after another in the field of science, Mysuru, too, is adding a new chapter to India's scientific journey in the form of this state-of-the-art COSMOS Planetarium. Today, this state-of-the-art COSMOS Planetarium is being dedicated to the youth and the people of the country. It is India's first LED Dome Planetarium. I have just had the opportunity to watch a show here. It was a remarkable experience in itself. I congratulate the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, the University of Mysore, various government departments and everyone associated with its construction. I extend my congratulations to the nation on this occasion.
Friends,
For a long time, there has been a call in our country, which Nirmala Ji mentioned in her speech just now - Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan. Atal Ji added Jai Vigyan to it, and then I added Jai Anusandhan as well. The India of the 21st century is moving forward with this very vision. And our country's youth are performing exceptionally well in this regard. Last year, India hosted the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics in Mumbai. Our young people participated in it with great enthusiasm. And this year, for the next edition of the same Olympiad, five students from India went to Vietnam. Four of them won gold medals and one won a silver medal. This is a matter of pride for the entire country.
Friends,
Our young students are also performing remarkably well in other fields of science. This year, Indian students achieved major successes in the International Olympiads as well. These included subjects such as Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology. All the students won either gold or silver medals. This has been a record achievement for India. This means that when our youth get opportunities, when they receive the necessary resources to learn, and when they get the support of technology, tools and institutions, they demonstrate their ability to achieve great things. This COSMOS Planetarium, too, is now going to help them greatly in giving shape to their dreams.
Friends,
Technology is changing the world very rapidly today. And no country can afford the risk of moving slowly in this area. Over the past decade, India has made unprecedented progress in astronomy, astrophysics and the space sector. We have installed new telescopes in the country. In several challenging areas of space exploration, India has today become one of the few countries in the world. Through Chandrayaan-3, ISRO made India the first country in the world to land near the Moon's South Pole. In the form of Aditya-L1, India has received its first solar observatory in space. Just last year, India became the fourth country in the world to demonstrate the capability of docking and undocking in space.
Friends,
During this period, an Indian also reached the International Space Station and conducted several new experiments. The experience gained from this mission is also proving useful for our own human spaceflight programme, Gaganyaan.
Friends,
Our government opened up the space sector. This created new opportunities for the private sector. India's startups also got an opportunity to demonstrate their capabilities. Today, our youth are launching their own rockets, placing satellites into orbit and undertaking many such activities in the space sector that had never been carried out in India before. This is the scientific approach of a New India, where new discoveries are being encouraged, new technologies are being developed and new opportunities are being created for our youth.
Friends,
India has always moved forward with the mantra of Humanity First. India's space missions, too, have been dedicated to the welfare of humanity. For example, ISRO has developed a satellite communication system for our fishermen brothers.
With the help of this system, when boats equipped with receivers are at sea, officials can send timely alerts to them during storms. And they can also track their safe return to the shore.
Friends,
Many of you must be checking the live location of trains. This tells you where a train has reached and when it is expected to arrive at a station. This information is provided by the Real-Time Train Tracking System developed by Indian Railways and ISRO. Similarly, satellite data is also used in the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana. Under this, information collected from fields, along with satellite data, is used to estimate crop yields. Farmers' insurance claims are being determined on the basis of these estimates. This means that today, our satellites are reaching the heights of space, while at the same time, they are being used to improve people's lives on Earth.
Friends,
Science for Society- this is our approach. We are continuously promoting research and innovation in the country. More than one crore students have so far benefited from the country's over 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs. These labs provide children with opportunities to work on their ideas, conduct new experiments and innovate.
Friends,
To advance research, it is essential that our students and researchers have access to the world's best research. With this objective, we launched One Nation One Subscription. It is now greatly helping the country's educational and research institutions gain access to leading scientific journals from around the world. We established the Anusandhan National Research Foundation. Through this, we are helping an increasing number of universities undertake new research.
Friends,
Last year, we also launched a Research, Development and Innovation Scheme worth Rs. 1 lakh crore, so that our country's researchers continue to receive adequate funding. This is helping take new technologies out of laboratories and bring them to practical use.
Friends,
Today, a strong ecosystem for science and research is taking shape in the country. Curiosity among young people is essential for making progress in the field of science. Planetariums and science centres play an important role in nurturing this curiosity. I urge everyone associated with COSMOS to work in this area so that schools and colleges here can organise visits for as many students as possible, and arrangements can be made to bring them here. The children who come here to learn about the universe may well be among those who return here one day and tell us about the new discoveries they have made about the universe. And that will be the greatest achievement of this COSMOS Planetarium. With this confidence, I wish you all the very best for the journey ahead. I extend my best wishes to all of you. Thank you very much.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi  inaugurates, dedicates to the nation, lays the foundation stone and flags off various development projects worth over ₹15,600 crore in Bengaluru, Karnataka
subtitle:
Infrastructure plays a vital role in the development journey of any nation; Better connectivity creates new avenues for progress, employment, and industry: PM

When developmental opportunities reach every section of society, the fight against poverty is further strengthened; It is a direct result of this that in recent years, nearly 50 crore citizens have emerged from extreme poverty: PM

Following Delhi-NCR and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Bengaluru has emerged as the third city in the nation where the metro network has achieved a century: PM

 The success of Namma Metro goes far beyond a single project; it is a powerful reflection of the country's new vision for Ease of Living and Ease of Travel: PM

Just a few days ago, Karnataka received the state's first-ever Vande Bharat Sleeper train; Today, it has been dedicated another Vande Bharat train that connects Karnataka to Goa: PM

Today, India is advancing with the objective of achieving leadership in emerging technologies, from chip to ship, and from AI and data centres to quantum computing: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 4:17PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated, dedicated to the nation, laid the foundation stone, and flagged off various development projects worth over ₹15,600 crore in Bengaluru, Karnataka. Addressing the gathering on the occasion, the Prime Minister extended his greetings in Kannada and bowed in reverence to the city's presiding deity Goddess Annamma Tai and Nadaprabhu Kempegowda, noting that today marks a day to give new momentum to the development journey of Bengaluru and Karnataka through projects spanning connectivity and energy security. “From projects connected with metro and rail to works of energy security, all these projects are going to give new strength to the infrastructure of Karnataka,” asserted Shri Modi.
Emphasizing that infrastructure and improved connectivity generate new avenues for progress, employment, and industry that reach every section of society and strengthen the fight against poverty, as reflected in nearly 50 crore citizens escaping extreme poverty in recent years, the Prime Minister extended his best wishes to the people of Karnataka for the newly launched projects. “They will give new momentum to the building of a Viksit Bharat through a Viksit Karnataka, and at the same time further strengthen the identity of Bengaluru as a Tech City,” affirmed PM Modi.
Highlighting the dedication of the Bengaluru Metro's new Pink Line a short while earlier, the Prime Minister noted that the corridor will significantly improve connectivity to IIM Bengaluru, numerous educational institutions, and major business, technology, and commercial hubs across the city. “Lakhs of people of Bengaluru will not only have convenience in commuting, rather they will also be able to save their money and time,” observed Shri Modi.
Recalling that yesterday marked the Punya Tithi of the late Ananth Kumar, who shared a deep bond with the region, the Prime Minister paid heartfelt tributes to the departed leader. “Seeing this metro line today, his soul too must have been delighted,” remarked PM Modi.
Describing Bengaluru as the Silicon Valley of India that contributes over one-third of the nation's IT exports and serves as a major engine of innovation and economic growth, the Prime Minister stated that the Central Government has prioritized the rapid development of the Bengaluru region and expanded Namma Metro from just 17 kilometers in 2014 to over 100 kilometers today, making Bengaluru the third Indian city after Delhi-NCR and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region to cross the 100-kilometer metro milestone. “This success of Namma Metro is the result of the country's new thinking regarding Ease of Living and Ease of Travel, and the outcome of the country's commitment to make the lives of middle-class families better,” asserted Shri Modi.
Stating that Indian Railways is shedding its colonial-era mindset to build a new legacy where stations, engines, and coaches bear India's distinct identity through Vande Bharat trains and Amrit Bharat stations, including over 60 stations in Karnataka alongside Chamarajanagar, Chikkamagaluru, Sakleshpur, and Subrahmanya Road, the Prime Minister highlighted how these stations blend modernity with sensitivity by offering special amenities for senior citizens and Divyangjans. “The facilities that were earlier found in airports, efforts are now being made to provide those very facilities at railway stations to poor and middle-class families,” noted PM Modi.
Pointing out that India's railway budget has grown manifold over the past 10 to 12 years with a ninefold increase in Karnataka's allocation, the Prime Minister noted that the state received four Amrit stations and two doubling and electrification projects today, alongside a new Vande Bharat train connecting Karnataka with Goa just days after receiving its first Vande Bharat Sleeper train. “Through this train, companions along the entire coastal route of Karnataka, including Mangaluru, will get a new experience of a semi-high-speed train,” observed Shri Modi.
Underscoring that the ongoing war around Iran and the Gulf region has demonstrated the vital importance of energy security, the Prime Minister explained that India weathered this challenging period firmly due to steps taken over the past decade, expanding petrol, diesel, and LPG production, crude oil storage, solar, hydro, and wind energy, near-total rail electrification, and metro networks, and detailed three new Karnataka projects: the Mangaluru LPG Project adding 80,000 metric tonnes of storage capacity, the Devangonthi Marketing Terminal streamlining petrol, diesel, and aviation fuel supply, and the Bengaluru CBG plant producing 13 tonnes of biogas daily. “This will improve waste management and money spent on the import of natural gas will also be saved,” noted PM Modi.
Highlighting that reliable electricity generation is essential as India strives for global leadership across new technologies from chips to ships and from AI and data centers to quantum computing, the Prime Minister noted that the nation is expanding its nuclear power plants to achieve clean energy goals. “Today India's renewable energy capacity has exceeded 300 gigawatts,” observed Shri Modi.
Pointing out that Central schemes are transforming Indian citizens from electricity consumers into electricity producers, the Prime Minister noted that over 60 lakh households nationwide, including more than 40,000 families in Karnataka, have installed rooftop solar plants with Central assistance of around 80,000 rupees per family under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, while irrigation through over 8 lakh solar pumps is being arranged for Karnataka's farmers under the PM KUSUM Yojana to cut power costs and generate new income and jobs. “Meaning, the Annadatas of Karnataka are now also becoming Urjadatas,” remarked PM Modi.
Observing that purposeful national execution, public participation, and proper utilization of taxpayer money under the post-2014 resolve of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas have expanded the middle class and created a new Aspirational Class seeking home appliances, two-wheelers, quality education, nutrition, healthcare, and tourism experiences, the Prime Minister pointed out that these rising aspirations are driving new industrial and job growth across automobiles, electronics, tourism, and services, making the Neo Middle Class a major engine of India's economic growth. “The interest of this Neo Middle Class, which is present in large numbers in Karnataka and in Bengaluru as well, is among the priorities of the Central Government,” affirmed Shri Modi.

date:

                13 NOV 2026 3:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Greetings to My Brothers and Sisters of Bengaluru! Governor of Karnataka, Sudha Yadav Ji, Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar Ji, Minister in the State Government, Krishna Byre Gowda Ji, and my colleague in the Lok Sabha, who have sent a brilliant young leader from Bengaluru, Tejasvi Surya Ji, other distinguished dignitaries present here, ladies and gentlemen.
This is the first occasion on which I have had the opportunity to share the stage at a programme with our Governor, Sudha Yadav Ji. Perhaps the people of Karnataka are not yet fully familiar with her. But I would certainly like to speak about her life. What does service to the nation mean? What does dedication to the nation mean? We can learn this from the life of Sudha Ji and her family. When the Kargil war was being fought, her husband was martyred in the war. Even after that, in the memory of her husband, she has continued to uphold her resolve to serve Mother India and has been working with a spirit of service to this day. Having served in Parliament for many years, she guided the nation on several important issues. And today, from the land of Karnataka, she is contributing towards the happiness, peace and prosperity of the people of Karnataka. I extend my very best wishes to Sudha Ji.
First of all, I respectfully pay my obeisance to Annamma Tai, the presiding deity of Bengaluru, and to Nada Prabhu Kempegowda Ji. This day is going to give a new impetus to the development journey of Bengaluru and Karnataka. Projects worth more than Rs. 15,000 crore, related to connectivity and energy security, are being launched from here today. From projects related to metro and railways to initiatives for energy security, all these projects will give new strength to Karnataka's infrastructure.
Friends,
Infrastructure plays a very important role in the development journey of any country. Better connectivity creates new opportunities for progress, employment and industries. And when these opportunities for development reach every section of society, the fight against poverty also becomes stronger. As a result, around 50 crore citizens of the country have come out of extreme poverty in recent years. The projects being launched today will also take this development journey forward. They will give a new impetus to the development of a Viksit Karnataka and, through a Viksit Karnataka, to the creation of a Viksit Bharat. They will also further strengthen Bengaluru's identity as a tech city. I extend my very best wishes to the people of Karnataka for all these projects.
Friends,
Just a short while ago, the new Pink Line of Bengaluru Metro was dedicated to the people of Bengaluru. With this new metro line, connectivity to IIM Bengaluru and several educational institutions will become even better. In addition, many areas that are known as major business, technology and commercial centres of Bengaluru will also be connected by the metro. This means that lakhs of people in Bengaluru will not only have greater convenience in commuting, but will also save both money and time.
Friends,
Yesterday was the death anniversary of the late Anant Kumar Ji. He had a special attachment to this region. Seeing this metro line today, his soul too must have felt delighted. I pay my heartfelt tributes to him.
Friends,
Bengaluru is India's Silicon Valley. It accounts for more than one-third of the country's IT exports. This city is a major engine of India's innovation and economic growth. Therefore, the rapid development of the entire Bengaluru region and the expansion of modern public transport are major priorities of the Central Government. With this vision, the Central Government is supporting the expansion of Namma Metro. In 2014, Namma Metro was only seventeen kilometres long. Today, its total network has grown to more than 100 kilometres. We are continuously scoring centuries. Shivakumar Ji, I was telling you: you may have heard a few days ago that India scored a century in Grandmasters Chess. India now has 100 chess grandmasters, and they have emerged during this very period.
Friends,
After Delhi-NCR and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Bengaluru has become the third city in the country to have a metro network of over 100 kilometres. This success of Namma Metro is not limited to just one project. It is the result of the country's new approach towards ease of living and ease of travel. It is the outcome of the country's commitment to improving the lives of middle-class families.
Friends,
Today, Indian Railways is leaving behind the old mindset of the era of slavery. The country's Railways is now creating a new heritage, a new legacy. Our railway stations, our railway engines and our railway coaches - everything now bears India's own imprint and identity. Vande Bharat trains and Amrit Bharat Stations are a glimpse of the railway services of Viksit Bharat. More than sixty railway stations in Karnataka, including Chamarajanagar, Chikkamagaluru, Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road stations, have also now become Amrit Bharat Stations. These stations reflect both sensitivity and modernity. Special facilities are available for every passenger, including senior citizens and persons with disabilities. An effort is being made to provide the same facilities at railway stations to poor and middle-class families that were earlier available at airports.
Friends,
Over the past 10–12 years, India's railway budget has increased several times over. During this period, as Tejasvi Ji has just mentioned, Karnataka's railway budget has also increased ninefold. Even today, Karnataka has received four Amrit Stations and two projects relating to doubling and electrification. A few days ago, Karnataka received its first Vande Bharat Sleeper train, and today Karnataka has received a Vande Bharat train connecting it with Goa. Through this train, people in Karnataka, including those in Mangaluru and along the entire coastal route, will get a new experience of travelling by a semi-high-speed train.
Friends,
Along with connectivity, energy security also plays a major role in the creation of Viksit Bharat. The ongoing war around Iran and the Gulf countries has shown how important energy security is. This has also been a challenging time for India. However, the steps taken over the past decade towards energy security have helped us face this crisis with strength. We have increased our capacity to produce petrol, diesel and LPG; developed arrangements for storing crude oil; expanded solar, hydro and wind energy; achieved almost 100 per cent electrification of the Railways; and strengthened public transport such as the metro. The three projects whose foundation stones have been laid or which have been inaugurated in Karnataka today will also give new strength to India's energy security. The LPG project in Mangaluru will increase the country's LPG storage capacity by 80,000 metric tonnes. The Devanagundi Marketing Terminal will make the supply of petrol, diesel and aviation fuel more organised and reliable. Meanwhile, the CBG plant in Bengaluru will produce around 13 tonnes of biogas every day. This will improve waste management and also save the money spent on importing natural gas.
Friends,
An important aspect of energy security is electricity generation. Today, India is moving forward with the goal of leadership in new technologies, from chips to ships, and from AI and data centres to quantum computing. Continuous efforts are also being made to ensure that the country has adequate electricity for this purpose. Today, India's renewable energy capacity has crossed 300 gigawatts. To achieve clean energy, India is also increasing the number of its nuclear power plants.
Friends,
Because of the schemes of the Central Government, today the citizens of India are becoming producers of electricity along with being consumers of electricity. Under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, more than 60 lakh families across the country have installed solar plants on their rooftops. These include more than 40,000 families in Karnataka as well. The Central Government has provided assistance of around Rs. 80,000 to each family. To every family. Similarly, under the PM-KUSUM scheme, arrangements are being made for irrigation through more than 8 lakh solar pumps for farmers in Karnataka. This means that the food providers of Karnataka are now also becoming energy providers. These schemes are reducing electricity expenses, while also creating new opportunities for income and employment.
Friends,
When a country moves forward with a mission, when every citizen becomes a part of development, and when the resources contributed by taxpayers are properly invested in development, the results are also encouraging and meaningful. In 2014, we began our work with the resolve of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas. Today, as a result of these very efforts, the middle class is expanding in the country, and a new Aspirational Class is emerging. This is a section of society whose aspirations are growing. It wants a refrigerator and a washing machine for its home. It wants a scooter or a motorcycle for its family. It wants to provide better education, nutrition and healthcare facilities to its children. It wants to spend on tourism and have new experiences. These growing aspirations are creating new demand in the country. From automobiles to electronics, and from tourism to the services sector, new industries, factories and employment opportunities are emerging. In other words, this neo-middle class is becoming a major engine of growth for India's economy. The interests of this neo-middle class, which is present in large numbers in Karnataka and Bengaluru as well, are among the priorities of the Central Government.
Friends,
The Central Government is continuously working to increase the savings of the middle class and put more money in their hands. We have exempted annual incomes of up to Rs. 12 lakh from income tax. By changing the TDS rules, we have provided relief to senior citizens and those earning rental income. Through the next-generation GST reforms, we have made everyday goods cheaper. By removing GST on personal health and life insurance, we have made insurance more affordable.
Friends,
Our effort is to increase the savings of the middle class, strengthen its purchasing power and enable it to fulfil its family's dreams while also contributing to the country's economic progress. The event being held in Karnataka today will also give a new impetus to this development journey. I extend my very best wishes to all of you for the new projects. Thank you very much to all of you!

content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram in Bengaluru, Karnataka. Addressing the gathering on the occasion, the Prime Minister greeted everyone in Kannada and expressed his joy at experiencing the remarkable energy of Yoga in Bengaluru. Noting that Karnataka has been a center of Yoga for centuries and the birthplace of numerous preceptors and scholars who enriched the tradition, he also recalled the contributions of legendary Kannada cinema icon Dr. Rajkumar. “Such practitioners of Yoga have also been here who, along with the world of art, also served Yoga,” remarked Shri Modi.
Describing Prashanti Kutiram's 50-year journey amid Karnataka's rich heritage as an unprecedented saga of service and dedication that every citizen should know, the Prime Minister highlighted its transformation from a modest center into a massive movement. “How an ordinary Yoga center transformed into such a massive movement is in itself an inspiration,” observed PM Modi.
Noting the inauguration of several new facilities at the campus during the milestone celebration, the Prime Minister extended his best wishes to the S-VYASA family for their ongoing initiatives. “I congratulate all of you, and the lakhs of Sadhaks associated with Prashanti Kutiram on the Golden Jubilee,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Paying reverent tributes to H. V. Seshadri on his birth centenary, which coincides with Prashanti Kutiram's Golden Jubilee this year, the Prime Minister stated that Seshadri ji dedicated his entire life to the mission of nation-building through character-building, recognizing that taking the country to the pinnacle of success requires dedicated, capable, and disciplined citizens.
Recalling H. V. Seshadri's simplicity, towering personality, vast experience, and deep humility in staying behind the scenes to elevate others, unite people, and prepare them for national service, the Prime Minister shared an example Seshadri ji often cited about learning from a mother who stays awake all night to nurture and serve her child selflessly. “If we expand this sentiment for society, then what great good will be done for society,” remarked Shri Modi.
Observing that H. V. Seshadri served society with the purity and selflessness of a mother, the Prime Minister expressed his good fortune in having continuously received Seshadri ji's affection and guidance. “The memories of the time spent with him and his words are still very precious to me today,” remarked PM Modi.
Recalling another unforgettable teaching of H. V. Seshadri, that when one gives to society with both hands, society gives back with lakhs of hands, the Prime Minister stated that he has witnessed this truth bear fruit repeatedly in his own life. “While serving  the public has always given me their blessings, and this is a very big asset of my life,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Pointing out that this same spirit of selfless service is evident across H. V. Seshadri's family, the Prime Minister lauded Dr. H. R. Nagendra and Dr. R. Nagarathna for carrying his mission forward through their dedicated work. “I appreciate every effort of theirs as well, and I felicitate them,” affirmed PM Modi.
Recalling the era when India was bound in the shackles of colonial rule and lakhs of freedom fighters battled for independence, the Prime Minister highlighted the parallel role played by national sages (Rashtra Rishis) like Swami Vivekananda in awakening the nation's spiritual consciousness. “He showed the youth of India the path of Yoga,” noted Shri Modi.
Stating that inspiration from sages like Swami Vivekananda gave birth to institutions like Prashanti Kutiram and S-VYASA, which not only connected the masses with Yoga but also conducted modern scientific research, trained practitioners, teachers, doctors, and philosophers serving globally, and built a holistic wellness ecosystem integrating Yoga, Ayurveda, naturopathy, and modern medicine, the Prime Minister praised their research on stress and lifestyle diseases. “The research work done in this direction has served the entire world, and I appreciate Prashanti Kutiram for these efforts,” remarked PM Modi.
Emphasizing that India has presented its culture, identity, and scientific heritage to the world with absolute confidence over the past 12 years, leading to the global observance of International Day of Yoga across Australia, Africa, and America with crores of participants and the entry of Yoga into schools, institutions, and workplaces worldwide, the Prime Minister noted that Saudi Arabia has recognized Yoga as a sports activity and its Sports Ministry signed an agreement with India's Ministry of AYUSH. “Examples of foreign nationals promoting Yoga continuously come to the fore, and the country is also enhancing their pride by honoring them with the Padma Shri,” observed Shri Modi.
Pointing out that growing global familiarity with Yoga sparks curiosity about India and an attraction toward its culture and traditional knowledge, opening new avenues of global connection through collective effort, the Prime Minister highlighted the parallel international expansion of Ayurveda. “In different countries of the world, more than 150 Ayurveda training courses have been recognized, and for cooperation in the expansion of Ayurveda, MoUs have been signed with 28 countries of the world,” noted PM Modi.
Stating that the government amended several rules alongside promoting Yoga so that the benefits of Yoga and Ayurveda reach every citizen, the Prime Minister highlighted that Yogasana has been recognized as a competitive sport in India and given a dedicated place in the Khelo India and National Games. “This change is very important for India, as pathways have also opened up for people connected with Yoga to participate in competitive tournaments,” asserted Shri Modi.
Detailing the government's sustained promotion of Ayurveda through the creation of a dedicated Ministry of AYUSH and support for Ayurvedic research and patents, which has propelled the AYUSH economy to lakhs of crores of rupees alongside rising herbal exports and growing global demand for Indian turmeric used for generations in households, the Prime Minister highlighted institutional steps to boost turmeric exports. “To give new strength to the production, quality, and export of turmeric, we have also constituted a National Turmeric Board,” noted PM Modi.
Emphasizing the need to share the benefits of India's ancient science and modern research with humanity while creating youth opportunities, the Prime Minister pointed to the launch of the e-AYUSH Visa facility to ease travel for foreign medical visitors and the establishment of the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre in Jamnagar. “Through this, research and international cooperation in traditional medicine are being promoted,” observed Shri Modi.
Noting that 140 crore citizens are working toward a Viksit Bharat energized by the latest World Bank report showing nearly 50 crore Indians escaped extreme poverty in 12 to 13 years, opening new avenues for families to prioritize health through Yoga with the support of Prashanti Kutiram, the Prime Minister urged the institution to draft a roadmap for new goals. “Prashanti Kutiram will also get the benefit of his youthful energy, and the country will also get it,” remarked PM Modi.

Seshadri Ji devoted his entire life to advancing the mission of ‘Nation Building through Individual Development’. He understood that if the country was to be taken to the pinnacle of success, it required dedicated, capable and disciplined citizens. Seshadri Ji devoted himself wholeheartedly to preparing such individuals. The goals he pursued while serving in the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh continue to inspire crores of Swayamsevaks even today.
Friends,
Whenever we remember him, the first image that comes to mind is his simple personality. Dattaji has just described his simplicity in such wonderful words. Such a towering personality, such vast experience, and yet such humility in his conduct! To remain in the background while encouraging others to move forward, to bring people together and prepare them for the nation-this was the great discipline of his life. During conversations, he would often cite an example. He used to say that we should learn from the conduct of a mother. Just as a mother stays awake throughout the night to serve her child, nurtures the child and works selflessly for the child, if we extend this very sentiment to society, imagine how much society would benefit.
Friends,
With the same selflessness as a mother, Seshadri Ji remained devoted to serving society. And I have been fortunate to receive his affection and guidance continuously. The memories of the time spent with him and his words remain invaluable to me even today.
Friends,
There is another thing that Seshadri Ji used to say which I can never forget. He would say that if we give to society with both our hands, society gives back to us with millions of hands. I have personally witnessed this principle bearing fruit time and again in my own life. While serving the people, the Janata Janardan, the people have always showered their blessings upon me, and this is one of the greatest assets of my life.
Friends,
We also see the same spirit of service in Seshadri Ji's family. Dr. Nagendra Ji and Dr. Nagarathna Ji are carrying forward his mission through their work. I appreciate all their efforts and extend my congratulations to them as well.
Friends,
When the country was shackled by the chains of colonial rule, millions of freedom fighters were fighting for independence on one hand, while on the other, great sages of the nation like Swami Vivekananda were awakening India's spiritual consciousness and showing the path of yoga to the youth of India.
Friends,
The inspiration drawn from sages like Swami Vivekananda gave rise to institutions such as Prashanti Kutiram. Here, an initiative was undertaken not only to connect yoga with the masses, but also to conduct new research by putting it to the test of modern science. This institution has not merely produced yoga practitioners; it has also prepared trainers and philosophers for society. These teachers, doctors and researchers are serving people across the country and the world through yoga. S-VYASA, which evolved from Prashanti Kutiram, has become an important institution in the fields of yoga education, scientific research and healthcare services. Along with yoga, you have also developed a holistic wellness ecosystem comprising facilities related to Ayurveda, naturopathy and modern medical science. The research work undertaken in areas such as stress-related challenges and lifestyle diseases has served the entire world. I commend Prashanti Kutiram for these efforts.
Friends,
Over the past 12 years, India has been presenting its culture, identity and knowledge systems to the world with complete confidence, and I say this with a sense of responsibility, with complete confidence. One outcome of this is that, at India's initiative, the entire world now celebrates International Yoga Day. On the occasion of Yoga Day, programmes related to yoga are organised across the world, from Australia to Africa and America. Crores of people participate in them. Today, in many countries across the world, yoga has reached our schools, institutions and workplaces. For instance, in Saudi Arabia, yoga has been recognised as a sporting activity. The Sports Ministry there has entered into an agreement with India's Ministry of AYUSH to promote yoga. We are continuously witnessing examples of foreign nationals promoting yoga. And I have personally experienced this. Wherever I travel across the world, during lunch or dinner, when I sit with foreign guests or Heads of State, there is hardly any lunch or dinner where yoga does not come up in the conversation. Earlier, I had to explain to them that I am not a yoga expert, but a practitioner. I then tell them about its various benefits, and they ask numerous questions. I have met many world leaders who tell me that their wives visit India once a year to learn yoga and teach yoga there. Some tell me that their daughters are learning yoga, while others say that their daughters have dedicated themselves to yoga. In the families of some of the world's most prominent Heads of State, there is someone or the other associated with yoga. This shows how far India has reached through yoga. It seems that yoga has become a gateway to understanding India. I have also seen foreign nationals, whether from the Royal Family of Qatar or from elsewhere, who are completely dedicated to yoga. India has also honoured many such individuals with the Padma Shri, thereby enhancing their prestige.
Friends,
As people across the world become more familiar with yoga, their curiosity to know India also grows. A new attraction develops towards our culture and traditional knowledge systems. This opens up a new avenue of engagement between India and the world. And all this has been made possible through our collective efforts. If I talk about Ayurveda, more than 150 Ayurveda training courses have been recognised in different countries across the world. Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) have been signed with 28 countries to facilitate cooperation in the expansion of Ayurveda.
Friends,
Our endeavour is to ensure that the benefits of Ayurveda and yoga reach every citizen of the country. Today, holistic healthcare has emerged as a new global movement. As a result, there is a natural attraction towards Ayurveda and naturopathy.
And friends,
When there is such excellence and enthusiasm all around, alongside promoting and propagating yoga, we have also made several changes to rules as per the requirements. In India, Yogasana has also been recognised as a competitive sport. New opportunities have been created for Yogasana in events such as Khelo India and the National Games. These changes are very significant for India. Just a few days ago, an international yoga competition was held in Ahmedabad. And I was amazed. When I visited Uzbekistan, they had secured the number one position in the world, and they had gathered all the winners and gold medallists there, who were citizens of that country. This shows that wherever I go, I see and meet people, yoga has become a subject of discussion everywhere. This has also opened up avenues for those associated with yoga to participate in competitive events.
Friends,
Just as with yoga, the Government of India is continuously promoting Ayurveda as well. There are many things in our country that do not receive the attention they deserve, even from well-informed people, including those who have an interest in these subjects. After so many years of independence, for the first time, a separate Ministry of AYUSH was established in the country. We have encouraged research related to Ayurveda and patents based on Ayurveda. And today, we are witnessing the results of these efforts. Exports of AYUSH and herbal products from India are continuously increasing. The economy associated with the AYUSH sector has grown to several lakh crore rupees. Our turmeric which Indian families have been using for generations in their food habits and household traditions, is now witnessing growing demand across the world. India is exporting turmeric in quantities that were once beyond imagination. Its exports have been continuously increasing. We have also established the National Turmeric Board to give a new impetus to the production, quality and exports of turmeric.
Friends,
We must also share the benefits of our ancient sciences and modern research with humanity and also realise the opportunities associated with these fields for our youth. With this objective, the Government has introduced the facility of an e-Ayush Visa. This is making it easier for people from abroad to come to India for treatment. The World Health Organization's (WHO) Global Centre for Traditional Medicine has been established in Jamnagar. Through this centre, research and international cooperation in traditional medicine are being promoted.
Friends,
Today, 140 crore citizens of the country are working continuously with a shared goal. And that goal is to build a Viksit Bharat! The latest World Bank report has given a new impetus to this mission. The World Bank report states that over the past 12–13 years, nearly 50 crore Indians-this is a very significant figure-have been lifted out of extreme poverty. New opportunities for a better life now lie ahead of these millions of families. The possibilities of adopting a healthy lifestyle and paying attention to their family's health have increased. Our endeavour is to make a healthy lifestyle a priority for every family. Yoga can play a very significant role in this, and I always say that yoga liberates us from diseases, and yoga also liberates us from indulgence. Moreover, it is the most effective health remedy that comes at zero cost. Prashanti Kutiram is part of this mission, and several new initiatives are also being undertaken by the institution. It has also been extending its support. Their contribution has been very valuable to this work. Therefore, I would like you to start preparing a roadmap for new goals from now onwards. Since I have come here, I will also entrust Dr. Nagendra Ji with a few tasks before I leave. Dr. Nagendra Ji has, in fact, written to me in a letter just a few days ago that he feels younger than ever before. And therefore, his youthful energy will benefit Prashanti Kutiram as well as the nation. However, I would like you to ensure that when Prashanti Kutiram completes 75 years, the country would have become a Viksit Bharat. So, keeping this vision of a Viksit Bharat in mind, start planning now for what your next 25 years should look like, and dedicate yourselves to this mission, so that the path you follow also contributes to strengthening the nation, and your journey towards the 75th year of Prashanti Kutiram, your next 25-year journey, also becomes a source of strength for a Viksit Bharat. I urge you all to think in this direction. With this conviction, I once again extend my congratulations to all of you on the Golden Jubilee celebrations. I also once again bow in reverence at the feet of the revered Seshadri Ji. Thank you very much to all of you!

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal inaugurates 45th India International Trade Fair 2026
subtitle:
IITF has emerged as a platform that brings together India’s states, businesses, products and capabilities: Shri Goyal

30 States and Union Territories showcasing their strengths, 3,500 exhibitors and participation from 11 countries at 45th IITF

India records all-time high exports of almost $90 billion in October 2026 showing strong resilience and growth: Shri Goyal
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 9:44PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today inaugurated the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, calling upon Indian businesses, manufacturers, exporters, artisans and entrepreneurs to leverage the opportunities created by India's Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and expand their presence in international markets. He emphasised that with markets across the developed world opening up for Indian goods and services, businesses must seize these opportunities and contribute to India's journey towards becoming a developed nation by 2047.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Goyal highlighted that India had recorded an all-time high in exports of nearly $90 billion in October 2026, comprising approximately $50 billion in merchandise exports and $40 billion in services exports. Describing this as a historic milestone, he said that India was well on track to achieve its $1 trillion export target in the current year. Exports during the first seven months up to October had reached $570 billion, an unprecedented achievement.
The Minister expressed confidence that India's international trade would grow by 15-16 per cent during the current year, despite two ongoing wars, global volatility and uncertainty, and subdued international trade growth, which is expected to remain around 3.5 per cent. He said India's performance reflected the strength of its economy, the confidence of its exporters and the country's ability to face global challenges with determination and self-respect.
Shri Goyal said that the 45th edition of IITF reflected five dimensions of Bharat: its economy, exports, infrastructure growth, the demand generated by 1.4 billion Indians and the country's rich diversity. He observed that the fair had evolved beyond an event focused largely on Delhi and had emerged as a platform bringing together India's states, businesses, products and capabilities.
Highlighting the new initiatives introduced at this year's fair, the Minister said that more than 30 States and Union Territories were showcasing their strengths, with over 3,500 exhibitors and participation from 11 countries. The One District, One Product Pavilion initiative, would showcase products from different parts of the country, highlighting India's strengths in arts, handicrafts, handloom and food products.
Another major attraction, the Hall of Inspiration, will showcase 600 startups and their innovations. The IITF mobile application will provide visitors with information about the entire fair, enabling them to navigate the exhibition and identify exhibitors of interest. Shri Goyal noted that visitors would need to set aside two to three days to explore the entire exhibition, given its extensive spread across Bharat Mandapam.
The Minister also announced that the Government would soon launch the next phase of expansion of Bharat Mandapam, which would almost double the available exhibition space for exhibitors. He said that the success of recent exhibitions, including IITF, had demonstrated that even the significantly expanded facilities available today were no longer adequate to meet growing demand.
Shri Goyal said that IITF would now be taken across the world, with the India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) planning several international fairs, both sector-specific and multi-dimensional. These fairs would provide Indian goods, services and startups opportunities to showcase their capabilities and engage with markets in developed countries and other international markets, particularly those with which India has entered into Free Trade Agreements. He called upon businesses and exhibitors to actively participate in these initiatives and contribute to India's global engagement.
Emphasising the importance of quality and sustainability, the Minister said that India's focus must remain on two key elements: quality and sustainability. Adopting the principle of Zero Defect, Zero Effect would help ensure equitable and inclusive growth across the country. He said every Made-in-India product must reflect high quality and reinforce India's reputation in international markets.
He further stressed the need to adopt high-quality standards in manufacturing and services while embracing sustainable practices, promoting a circular economy, using natural products and giving greater importance to biodegradable products. He said that ensuring economic growth without damaging the environment would position India as a global winner in the race to capture international markets and improve the prosperity of its people.
Highlighting the growing strength of India's domestic economy, Shri Goyal referred to the strong business activity witnessed during the recent festive season, including Diwali, Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj, as well as Navratri, Dussehra and Dhanteras. He said that stores across the country had witnessed significant consumer demand and business activity had been considerably higher. The October GST collections had already registered an all-time high for the month, and he expressed confidence that November would also witness record collections.
The Minister said that these developments reflected the strength of India's growth story, with every section of the economy contributing to the country's progress. Farmers, fishermen, workers, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), manufacturers, service providers, artists, artisans and handloom and handicraft producers were all demonstrating growth and confidence. From neighbourhood kirana stores and e-commerce businesses to artisans and major brands, every segment was looking to benefit from the expanding economic opportunities.
He observed that India's young entrepreneurs and businesses were increasingly reaching out to global markets, expanding production and looking towards a brighter future. Citing examples of emerging export opportunities, he referred to the export of Kiwi from Arunachal Pradesh, where exports had earlier been negligible, and Sindhuri pomegranates from Kullu reaching Dubai. He urged exhibitors and businesses at IITF to identify products with export potential and take advantage of the opportunities available through India's FTAs, emphasising that international markets were now open and Indian businesses must take the initiative to access them.
Shri Goyal said that India's growth was being powered by a young population aspiring for a better quality of life, improved education and healthcare, and greater opportunities to develop skills and talent. He noted that India had, in a span of 12 years, brought nearly 50 crore people, or 500 million people, out of extreme poverty. This had created a sense of achievement as well as aspirations for a brighter future among people across the country.
He said India was confidently facing global adversities, remaining focused on commerce, economic growth and the well-being of its people, irrespective of conflicts and uncertainties around the world. He attributed this confidence to decisive leadership and the country's growing economic strength.
Referring to India's long-term economic ambitions, the Minister said that the country's current four trillion dollar economy aspired to become a $30 trillion economy by 2047, when India would celebrate 100 years of Independence. He said that the country's young population, expanding businesses and growing export capabilities would play an important role in achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat.
The Minister also underlined the importance of preserving India's heritage and traditions while pursuing development. He said that the theme of this year's IITF aptly reflected the India story, as development remained incomplete without respect for heritage. Referring to the experience of developed nations, he observed that countries which had achieved prosperity had also protected, encouraged and promoted their traditions, heritage and culture.
The Minister also referred to the recently approved establishment of the world's largest museum, the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum, in the North Block and South Block complex. He said that  Honourable Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi recognised the importance of presenting India's diversity, long history, contributions to the world over several thousand years, rich cultural heritage and traditions to the global community. Referring to the fact that India had once contributed more than 30 per cent to the global economy, Shri Goyal said that understanding and recognising the country's past was essential to reclaiming its rightful position in the comity of nations and realising the vision of a developed India.
He expressed confidence that the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum, being developed at the North Block and South Block complex, would showcase India's history, traditions and contributions to the world and serve as a source of inspiration for future generations, particularly the country's youth.
Shri Goyal said that the 45th IITF had moved beyond incremental improvements and taken a significant leap towards the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. He expressed confidence that the fair would become a trendsetter and mark the beginning of a new era in how India presented itself to the world and engaged with international markets to promote Indian goods, services, arts and culture.
He said that initiatives led by ITPO and the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, in coordination with State Governments and other Central Government Ministries through a whole-of-government approach, would create greater opportunities for Indian businesses and entrepreneurs across the world.
Concluding his address, Shri Goyal declared the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026 open and called upon all stakeholders to actively contribute to India's journey of economic progress and global engagement.

title: CCPA Imposes ₹10 Lakh Penalty on Ola for Pre-Ride ‘Tip’ Feature; Directs Platform to Discontinue Practice
subtitle: Authority finds Ola's advance payment prompts misleading; holds the practice to be an unfair trade practice and a dark pattern
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 1:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of
₹10 lakh
on
ANI Technologies Private Limited
, which operates the ride-hailing platform Ola, for soliciting additional payments from consumers before completion of their journeys through its pre-ride ‘tip’/‘add-on’ feature. The Authority has directed Ola to immediately discontinue the practice, holding that it misleads consumers, constitutes an unfair trade practice and employs a dark pattern.
The order was passed by the CCPA, headed by Chief Commissioner Smt. Nidhi Khare and Commissioner Shri Anupam Mishra, following an examination of the feature that prompted consumers to make an additional payment while the app was searching for a driver, suggesting that it could improve their chances of securing a ride faster. Although
Ola subsequently renamed the ‘tip’ as an ‘add-on’, the underlying practice remained unchanged
.
The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a ₹10 lakh penalty on Ola for misleading pre-ride payment prompts and directed the discontinuation of the feature. A firm step against dark patterns, unfair practices and misleading claims, reaffirming the commitment to protecting consumer rights and ensuring transparency.

ಕೇಂದ್ರ ಗ್ರಾಹಕ ರಕ್ಷಣಾ ಪ್ರಾಧಿಕಾರವು (CCPA), ಓಲಾ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಯ ರೈಡ್‌ಗೆ ಮುನ್ನವೇ ಪಾವತಿ ಮಾಡುವಂತೆ ಗ್ರಾಹಕರನ್ನು ದಾರಿ ತಪ್ಪಿಸುವ ಸೂಚನೆಗಳನ್ನು ನೀಡಿದ್ದಕ್ಕಾಗಿ, ಓಲಾ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಗೆ ₹10 ಲಕ್ಷ ದಂಡ ವಿಧಿಸಿದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಈ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಯನ್ನು ತಕ್ಷಣವೇ ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸುವಂತೆ ಆದೇಶಿಸಿದೆ. 'ಡಾರ್ಕ್ ಪ್ಯಾಟರ್ನ್‌ಗಳು', ಅನಗತ್ಯ ಹಾಗೂ ಅನ್ಯಾಯದ ಪದ್ಧತಿಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ದಾರಿ ತಪ್ಪಿಸುವ ಕ್ರಮಗಳ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಕೈಗೊಂಡಿರುವ ಈ ಕಠಿಣ ಕ್ರಮವು, ಗ್ರಾಹಕರ ಹಕ್ಕುಗಳನ್ನು ರಕ್ಷಿಸುವ ಹಾಗೂ ಪಾರದರ್ಶಕತೆಯನ್ನು ಖಚಿತಪಡಿಸುವ ಬದ್ಧತೆಯನ್ನು ಪುನರುಚ್ಚರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

#CCPA 
@jagograhakjago
— Pralhad Joshi (@JoshiPralhad)
November 12, 2026
Additional payment prompts created a misleading impression of faster ride confirmation
The CCPA examined the different versions of the Ola app interface and found that messages such as
“Adding a tip might help increase the chances of getting a ride faster”
,
“Tip now to boost the chances of getting a ride sooner”
and
“Improve your chances of quicker ride confirmation!”
suggested that paying extra would help consumers secure a ride faster.
The Authority observed that these messages appeared while the app was searching for a driver and directly above pre-set payment amounts. This created the impression that an additional payment could speed up the booking process. The use of qualifying words such as ‘might’ and ‘chance’ did not alter the overall impression conveyed to consumers.
Ola's own booking data for 1–15 June 2026 did not support this claim. Ride requests carrying an add-on were accepted less frequently than those without one:
City
With add-on
Without add-on
Delhi
38%
62%
Bengaluru
40%
68%
Mumbai
39%
68%
The Authority also noted that Ola's position was contradictory. While the company stated that the add-on did not influence ride allocation, its app suggested that paying extra could improve the chances of getting a ride sooner.
Further, consumers were not informed that the platform's own data showed lower acceptance rates for requests carrying an add-on or the basis on which the suggested payment amounts were generated.
The CCPA held that these omissions amounted to concealment of material information under Section 2(28)(iv) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
CCPA holds advance tipping to be an unfair trade practice
The Authority observed that a tip is ordinarily a voluntary payment made after a service has been provided. Soliciting it before the journey effectively converts a voluntary gratuity into a pre-service payment. Merely renaming the feature from ‘tip’ to ‘add-on’ did not change the nature of the practice.
The CCPA further noted that:
The additional payment was solicited after consumers had already booked a ride at an upfront fare, which accounts for peak pricing and the driver's distance to the pick-up point. Seeking another payment on account of the same supply constraints amounted to charging an additional premium.
The suggested amounts were generated by the platform on an undisclosed basis. These amounts increased from ₹10–₹40 in May 2025 to as much as ₹140, while the interface permitted payments of up to ₹499.
Consumers could not independently verify the need for an additional payment, as information regarding driver availability was controlled by the platform.
Making an additional payment appear necessary for timely acceptance of a ride that had already been booked also raised concerns of an unfair contract.
The practice was also found to be contrary to Clause 14.15 of the Motor Vehicles Aggregators Guidelines, 2025, which provides for a tipping feature only after completion of the journey. The Authority noted that Ola continued displaying the prompt even after the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways clarified on 11 August 2026 that such prompts could not be displayed before completion of the ride.
Under Section 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019
, an unfair trade practice includes the use of unfair or deceptive methods and false or misleading representations regarding the benefits or usefulness of a service. The CCPA held that Ola's additional payment prompts fell within this provision.
Interface design used ‘Confirm Shaming’ to encourage additional payments
The CCPA also examined the feature under the Guidelines for
Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023.
The prompts appeared when consumers were waiting for a driver to accept their booking. By suggesting that an additional payment would improve their chances of securing a ride, the interface implied that consumers who did not pay could face delays or might not get a ride. The Authority held that this created a sense of fear and amounted to
‘Confirm Shaming’
, as specified under Clause 3 of Annexure 1 to the Guidelines.
The Authority further observed that:
Pre-set payment amounts displayed below the prompt anchored consumers to higher figures.
The message
“Generous Add On!”
further encouraged consumers to make an additional payment.
The interface did not provide an option to close the prompt.
The prompt appeared after the ride had already been booked, when consumers were waiting for confirmation and had limited information about driver availability or the likely impact of making an additional payment.
The Authority also noted that Ola's booking data reflected such requests from hospitals, railway stations, inter-state bus terminals and airports. Consumers such as patients, elderly persons, travellers carrying luggage and individuals travelling alone or at night could be particularly vulnerable to such prompts.
Ola directed to discontinue all pre-ride payment prompts and pay ₹10 lakh penalty
The CCPA has directed Ola to:
Immediately discontinue all prompts, messages, pre-set amounts and interface designs that solicit any payment, whether described as a tip, add-on, additional fare or by any other name, over and above the upfront fare before completion of the journey.
Ensure strict compliance with the Consumer Protection Act, 2019; the Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023; and the Guidelines for Prevention of Misleading Advertisements and Endorsements for Misleading Advertisements, 2022.
Pay a penalty of ₹10 lakh.The CCPA has also taken suo motu action against other cab aggregator platforms concerning the same practice. It has earlier passed an order against Rapido (Roppen Transportation Services Pvt. Ltd.), imposing a penalty of ₹10 lakh. Proceedings against Uber and Namma Yatri are currently under investigation.
Consumers who encounter such practices or face difficulties in accessing services can register their complaints through the National Consumer Helpline at
1915
or write to
com-ccpa@gov.in
.
The
Final Order
is available on the CCPA website.
