title: Ministry of Culture Convenes "Creative India: Collective Possibilities" at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi; Invites Partners to Build India's Creative Economy Together
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 5:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Culture, Government of India, today organised "
Creative India: Collective Possibilities
", a conference on collaborative models for India's creative economy, at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Inaugurated by
Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
, Hon'ble Union Minister for Culture, the Conclave brought together representatives of the Central and State Governments, the Ministry's institutions, industry, philanthropy, the creative community and international partners, to explore how India's cultural wealth can contribute more fully to growth, livelihoods and India's place in the world.
"
The creative power of India is its real power,"
said Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat. "Ours is a living civilisation, whose creativity belongs to every region and every generation. As the world turns to an economy of ideas and imagination, our task is to connect this talent with opportunity, so that India's culture becomes a foundation of its prosperity and of its voice in the world."
"Government's role is to be a catalyst," said
Shri Vivek Aggarwal
, Secretary, Ministry of Culture. "When the Ministry opens the door and partners carry the work forward, our heritage becomes a living resource for communities, artists and enterprise alike. The Creative Economy Division has been created to build exactly these partnerships."
Setting the context,
Shri Inderjeet Singh
, IAS, Joint Secretary (Creative Economy), placed culture at the heart of India's development agenda, from the Kashi Culture Pathway to the vision of Viksit Bharat. He described the Ministry's 43 organisations, from more than 3,600 protected monuments to museums, archives, Akademis and Zonal Cultural Centres, as the public infrastructure of India's creative economy. As custodian of India's heritage, collections and living traditions, he said, the Ministry offers a natural meeting point for the many sectors, enterprises and creators that draw on India's culture.
Partnerships are already in motion. The
National Culture Fund
has completed 66 projects with 39 partners since 1996, and Adopt a Heritage engages partners at 66 monuments. The sacred Piprahwa relics returned home through a partnership with Godrej Industries Group, Sabhyata Foundation has brought cultural evenings to Purana Qila, and the India Pavilion at Venice 2026 was realised with the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre and Serendipity Arts Foundation. A new MoU with Google Arts & Culture will carry India's heritage to audiences worldwide.
Four sessions, on
Investing in Culture, Culture-Led Spaces, Culturepreneurs, and Technology and Communication
, brought patrons, investors, heritage practitioners, designers, entrepreneurs and technology leaders into conversation. The deliberations explored trusted routes for philanthropy and private capital, monuments, museums and festivals as living destinations, pathways from livelihood to enterprise for artisans and designers, and new ways of carrying India's knowledge and narratives to the world on India's own terms.
The takeaways from the day will inform the Ministry's continued engagement with States, institutions and partners, in India and abroad.
The Ministry envisages a common and evolving framework for India's creative economy, grounded in measurable outcomes, simpler facilitation and structured routes for capital into culture. Guided by the principle of convening, facilitating and enabling, the Ministry invited its partners, from State Governments and cultural institutions to industry, philanthropy, creators and the international community, to shape this framework with it and to work with its institutions in turning India's heritage and living traditions into lasting livelihoods, enterprise and global presence.

title: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda reviews institutional progress of Rural Health Training Centre (RHTC), Najafgarh
subtitle:
Shri J.P. Nadda Commends RHTC Najafgarh for Its Commendable Progress and Strengthening of Institutional Infrastructure and Healthcare Services

RHTC records over 94,900 OPD visits and nearly 36,000 emergency cases between August and October 2026

Centre strengthens primary healthcare network through three Urban Primary Health Centres and their Sub-Centres
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 5:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda today reviewed the institutional progress and development of the Rural Health Training Centre (RHTC), Najafgarh, New Delhi, under the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
During the review, the Minister was apprised of the progress made by the institution across hospital and patient care services, diagnostic and support facilities, human resources, academic infrastructure, quality assurance and community-based healthcare delivery.
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda appreciated the commendable work undertaken by RHTC Najafgarh in strengthening its institutional infrastructure and healthcare services. He observed that the institution was progressing in the right direction and commended the efforts of the RHTC team in taking forward its development initiatives. He also acknowledged the significant contribution of Safdarjung Hospital and the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in supporting the institution's growth and development. He expressed confidence that the continued efforts and collective commitment of all stakeholders would further strengthen RHTC as an important centre for patient care, medical education and community healthcare.
Strengthening Hospital and Patient Care Services
RHTC Najafgarh has recorded substantial patient footfall during the August–October 2026 period. The institution attended to 94,927 patients in its Outpatient Department (OPD) across 10 specialities and provided emergency services to 35,985 patients. The hospital recorded 198 inpatient admissions during this period.
The institution also performed 691 surgeries, comprising 101 major and 590 minor surgeries. Its Anti-Rabies Centre and the Snake Bite Treatment facility also provided substantial service during the same time span.
The hospital has functional labour rooms, a pharmacy with an updated formulary of over 350 medicines, and dedicated Ayurvedic and Dental Clinics, further broadening the range of services available to patients.
Expansion of Diagnostic and Support Infrastructure
The review also highlighted the strengthening of diagnostic and support services at the institution. The laboratory is NABL-accredited, while the Ultrasound (USG) facility became operational on October 24, 2026, and has conducted 148 scans. The Physiotherapy and Audiometry units are functional, with 252 audiometry tests conducted between August and October 2026.
Other important facilities, including the Central Sterile Supply Department (CSSD), Effluent Treatment Plant, Sewage Treatment Plant and Medical Gas Pipeline System, have also been completed.
The institution is working towards operationalising the Blood Storage Unit and Mortuary by January 2027. The CT Scan and X-ray facilities are planned to become operational during the first quarter of 2027.
Focus on Academic Infrastructure and Quality Assurance
RHTC has also strengthened its nursing education and training infrastructure. The ANM Training School has been renovated, with an annual intake capacity of 44 students for its two-year course. The institution also has an ANM hostel with a capacity of 60 beds.
The institution has undertaken quality improvement initiatives under the National Quality Assurance Standards (NQAS) for its three Urban Primary Health Centres. Of the 129 identified action points, 105 have been completed, while 24 are in progress. State-level evaluation and certification are targeted for December 2026, followed by national-level evaluation from February 2027 onwards.
The institution has also completed several important compliance-related activities, including biomedical waste management certification from the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC), e-waste management and Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) compliance. Energy, fire, structural and safety audits have been completed, while the water audit is in progress.
Future Development Roadmap
The review also covered the institution's short-, medium- and long-term development plans. In the short term, RHTC aims to operationalise specialised clinics, including Thalassemia, De-addiction, Adolescent Health, Venereal Disease, Rheumatology and Non-Communicable Disease clinics by December 2026.
The medium-term roadmap envisages the establishment of teaching departments in Family Medicine and Emergency Medicine, with a target of operationalisation by the end of the first quarter of 2027. The longer-term vision includes the development of a B.Sc. Nursing College, Allied Health Sciences College, residential hostel and expansion of medical education facilities.
The process of upgrading RHTC into a 230-bedded hospital is already underway. The proposed expansion is expected to strengthen its capacity for patient care, medical education and institutional training.
The review also covered key operational requirements, including the availability of specialists, senior residents and other healthcare personnel, along with infrastructure and administrative matters necessary for the institution's further development.
About RHTC
Established in 1937, RHTC Najafgarh has a longstanding legacy of service, education and community healthcare. The institution provides comprehensive primary healthcare services through three Urban Primary Health Centres (UPHCs) at Najafgarh, Ujwa and Palam, along with their respective Sub-Centres. These facilities cater to the healthcare needs of the rural and peri-urban population, with a focus on maternal and child health, immunisation, family welfare and disease control programmes. The centres also serve as practical training facilities for medical, nursing and paramedical students.
The progress at RHTC Najafgarh reflects the continued efforts towards strengthening accessible, comprehensive and quality healthcare services, while developing institutions that integrate patient care, medical education, skill development and community health.

title: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Highlights India's Remarkable Progress in Reducing TB Mortality; Reiterates Resolve for TB-Mukt Bharat
subtitle:
WHO South-East Asia Region Recognises India's Significant Contribution to Reducing TB Mortality Across the Region

India Records Its Highest-Ever 38% Reduction in TB Mortality Since 2015, Outperforming Global Decline of 35%: WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026

India's 94% TB Treatment Success Rate Reflects Strengthened Diagnosis, Timely Treatment and Comprehensive Patient Care

Under PM Modi's Leadership, India's Fight Against TB Has Become a Nationwide Jan Andolan Driven by Technology, Community Participation and Patient-Centric Care: Shri J.P. Nadda

TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Reaches Over 25 Crore People; More Than 11 Crore Chest X-Rays and 3 Crore Molecular Tests Conducted

Nearly 15 Lakh Asymptomatic TB Cases Detected Through Intensified Screening, Enabling Early Diagnosis and Timely Treatment
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 2:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda has underscored India's significant progress in the fight against tuberculosis (TB), following the release of the World Health Organization's (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report 2026, which highlights a 38% reduction in TB mortality since 2015, surpassing the global decline of 35%, and a 94% treatment success rate among patients with drug-susceptible TB.
Describing the results as encouraging, the Union Health Minister reaffirmed the Government's commitment to ensuring that no TB patient is left behind, while emphasising the importance of technology, community participation and comprehensive patient care in accelerating progress towards a TB-Mukt Bharat.
In a significant acknowledgement of India's achievements, the World Health Organization's South-East Asia Regional Office (WHO SEARO) has also recognised the country's contribution to reducing TB mortality across the region.
In a social media post, WHO SEARO stated, "India is making a significant contribution to the progress in reducing tuberculosis mortality in the WHO South-East Asia Region." The organisation also shared the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare's announcement on India's achievements highlighted in the WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026.
In his message, Shri Nadda emphasised that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India's fight against tuberculosis has transformed into a nationwide
Jan Andolan, powered by technology, community participation and patient-centric care
. He highlighted how sustained investments in early detection, advanced diagnostics, nutritional assistance and community mobilisation have strengthened the country's TB elimination efforts.
Drawing attention to the scale of the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, the Union Health Minister stated that over
25 crore people have been covered under intensified TB screening
, with more than
11 crore chest X-rays and 3 crore molecular tests
conducted. These efforts have led to the detection of
48.64 lakh TB cases, including nearly 15 lakh asymptomatic cases
, enabling early diagnosis and timely initiation of treatment.
Shri Nadda also highlighted the role of AI-enabled diagnostics, nutritional assistance under the Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana and the dedicated efforts of Ni-kshay Mitras in strengthening TB care and improving patient support.
Reaffirming the Government's resolve, the Union Health Minister stated that these achievements reinforce the commitment to ensuring that
no TB patient is left behind
. He emphasised that sustained Jan Bhagidari and collective efforts would remain central to India's journey towards a TB-Mukt Bharat.
The WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 documents India's highest-ever reduction in estimated TB mortality, with the mortality rate declining from
28 deaths per lakh population in 2015 to 18 deaths per lakh in 2025
. The 94% treatment success rate among patients with drug-susceptible TB further reflects improvements in diagnosis, treatment delivery, patient follow-up and comprehensive support under the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP).
India's progress has been supported by a sustained shift towards proactive case finding, technology-enabled screening and patient-centred care. The TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, initially launched as an intensified 100-day campaign in December 2024 and subsequently expanded nationwide, has strengthened outreach among vulnerable and high-risk populations. A further intensified campaign launched in March 2026 has continued this focus on early detection and timely treatment.
The identification of
14.97 lakh asymptomatic TB cases
is particularly significant, demonstrating the effectiveness of proactive screening in detecting infections among individuals who may not exhibit typical symptoms. Such early detection provides opportunities for prompt treatment, reducing the risk of disease progression and further transmission.
Technological innovations, including AI-enabled portable digital chest X-rays, rapid molecular diagnostic technologies and the Ni-kshay digital platform, have strengthened TB screening, diagnosis and treatment monitoring. These interventions are complemented by nutritional assistance under the Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana and community support through the Ni-kshay Mitra initiative, which help address the broader needs of people undergoing TB treatment.
Community participation has emerged as a defining feature of India's TB response. In 2025,
67,933 Panchayats were declared TB-free
, reflecting growing grassroots involvement in the national elimination effort. The JOSH Teams initiative is further expanding community engagement by bringing together government officials, NCC cadets and MY Bharat volunteers to support awareness generation, outreach and mobilisation at the local level.
India's commitment to TB elimination is also reflected in
96% of programme funding requirements being met through domestic resources
, demonstrating sustained national investment and strong ownership of the country's TB response.
The recognition by WHO SEARO, together with the findings of the WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026, brings into focus India's contribution to reducing TB mortality and advancing regional and global efforts against the disease. The progress reflects the combined impact of expanded access to healthcare, scientific innovation, strengthened programme implementation and active community participation.
Building on these gains, the Government of India remains committed to further strengthening TB prevention, early diagnosis, timely and effective treatment, nutritional support and community engagement. Guided by the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and supported by the collective participation of States and Union Territories, healthcare professionals, development partners and citizens, India continues to advance towards the goal of a TB-Mukt Bharat.

title: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs Special Campaign 6: 736 Public Grievances Redressed, 448 MP References Disposed of and 25,070 Files Reviewed
subtitle:
526 cleanliness campaigns conducted; 10,551 square feet of office space freed

Scrap disposal generates ₹2.50 lakh; 100 percent PMO references disposed of
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 4:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Special Campaign 6, undertaken during October 2026 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs  recorded significant achievements in reducing administrative pendency, strengthening record management and promoting cleanliness in government offices. The campaign focused on the disposal of pending references, redressal of public grievances, review of physical and electronic files, simplification of rules and processes, and management of e-waste.
Disposal of Pending References and Redressal of Public Grievances
As on 31 October 2026,
736 public grievances were redressed
,
448 references from Members of Parliament were disposed of
, and
100 Percent PMO references were disposed of
. In addition, seven Parliamentary Assurances were addressed and one State Government reference was disposed of.
These activities formed part of the campaign’s efforts to reduce pendency and promote responsive administration.
Review of 25,070 Files to Strengthen Record Management
A total of
25,070 files were reviewed
, comprising
16,217 physical files and 8,853 e-files
. The exercise supported systematic management of official records and identification of files for retention or disposal in accordance with applicable procedures.
526 Cleanliness Campaigns Conducted; 10,551 Square Feet of Space Freed
During the campaign,
526 cleanliness campaigns were conducted
to promote cleaner and better-organised workplaces.
Disposal of scrap and obsolete materials, along with weeding out of old files, freed
10,551 square feet of office space
, making it available for more effective utilisation.
Scrap Disposal Generates ₹2.50 Lakh
The campaign generated
₹2,49,656 in revenue through disposal of scrap, including e-waste
. Of this amount,
₹40,036 was generated through e-waste disposal
.
E-waste management activities covered
77 units
, supporting efforts towards responsible disposal of obsolete electronic materials.
Four Rules and Processes Identified for Simplification
As part of the drive to improve administrative efficiency,
four rules and processes were identified for simplification
.
Special Campaign 6 reinforced the importance of integrating cleanliness, timely disposal of pending matters and systematic record management into routine office functioning. The campaign’s achievements reflect continued efforts towards efficient use of public resources and responsive, citizen-centric governance.

The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 will showcase
I Matter

Gala Premieres
The Gala Premieres segment will feature 14 screenings, with participation from 87 countries showcasing a curated selection of films and providing audiences an opportunity to experience diverse cinematic stories and acclaimed filmmaking.
The Country of Honour: Spain
The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) highlights Spain as the Country of Honour, showcasing four Spanish films: The Bad Son, directed by Jaime Lorente; Trinidad; Bitter Christmas, directed by Pedro Almodóvar; and Persegiuiendo a Michael, directed by Jaime Machia. The selection celebrates Spanish cinema and its diverse storytelling, bringing Spanish filmmakers and cinematic perspectives to the international platform of IFFI.
Partner Country: Russia
The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) presents Russia as the Partner Country, with a special showcase of four films representing the diversity and creative richness of Russian cinema. The featured films include Four (Четыре), New Home, Bo Bo, directed by Anastasia Kuzina, and Sidney Lumet’s Birthday. The showcase provides Indian and international audiences with an opportunity to discover contemporary Russian filmmaking, engage with its evolving cinematic landscape and appreciate the cultural and artistic exchange between India and Russia through the medium of cinema.
IFFI 2026 Introduces Two New Segments
The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 has introduced two new segments this year to broaden its cinematic offerings and celebrate diverse forms of storytelling. The first segment,
Animation
, will feature five outstanding films, showcasing creativity and innovation in animated cinema. The second segment,
Films About Films
, will also present five films and has been introduced in response to suggestions from renowned filmmakers, with the objective of bringing the art and craft of filmmaking to the forefront.
IFFI 2026 Places Special Focus on BRICS Cinema
Another key highlight of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 will be its special focus on BRICS cinema. India’s
Ramayana
will be the opening film of the BRICS segment, which will showcase films from all 11 member countries, along with contributions from partner countries, offering audiences an opportunity to explore diverse cinematic traditions and storytelling from across the BRICS nations.
Indian Panorama
Total 76 films are being showcased under Indian Cinema section in 18 diffrent languages, reflecting the country’s diverse storytelling traditions and creative excellence.
The selection process received 404 feature film submissions& the non-feature category received 358 submissions. The Best Web Series (OTT) category received 46 eligible entries.
‘Dhurandhar’ and ‘Becoming’ to Open Indian Panorama at IFFI 2026
The Indian Panorama section of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 will open with
Dhurandhar
, a Hindi feature film, and
Becoming
, a Ladakhi-language non-feature film. Bringing together films from two distinct linguistic and cinematic backgrounds, the opening selection reflects IFFI’s vision of celebrating India’s diverse storytelling traditions and showcasing cinema without borders.
Best Debut Feature Films Competition
The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) presents the Best Debut Feature Films Competition, featuring seven films from different countries, celebrating emerging filmmakers and fresh cinematic perspectives from across the world. The competition includes Fading Man from Germany, The Sledge from India, Paris from Belgium, The Black Sea from Egypt, L’Âge d’Or (The Golden Age) from France and Italy, Birds on Ice from India, and Atlantic from China. The competition provides an international platform for first-time feature film directors to showcase their talent, gain wider recognition and connect with global audiences, while highlighting IFFI’s commitment to encouraging new voices and nurturing the next generation of filmmakers.
Women Filmmakers, Debut Voices & Emerging Talent
Celebrating fresh perspectives and diverse storytelling, the 57th IFFI will bring together
52 women filmmakers and 62 debut filmmakers
, reflecting the expanding creative landscape of Indian and international cinema. The competitive sections will further spotlight
10 women filmmakers and 12 debut filmmakers
, underscoring the festival’s commitment to amplifying women’s voices, nurturing new talent and providing a global platform for the next generation of cinematic storytellers.
Creative Minds of Tomorrow (CMOT)
The sixth edition of Creative Minds of Tomorrow will bring together 100 selected participants across 13 filmmaking crafts.
The programme will feature specially curated masterclasses, workshops, in-conversation sessions, a 48-hour filmmaking challenge and the CMOT Talent Camp. Participants will engage with leading filmmakers and industry professionals, pitch creative concepts and explore opportunities across the media and entertainment industry.
WAVES Film Bazaar
WAVES Film Bazaar will bring together filmmakers, producers, buyers, distributors and industry stakeholders to facilitate collaboration, co-production and business opportunities.
The Bazaar will welcome 150 invited guests, including buyers and production houses. Its key initiatives will include the Screenwriters’ Lab, Co-production Market, Viewing Room and Work-in-Progress Lab.
Netflix, the Knowledge Series partner at WAVES Bazaar, will support industry capacity-building and showcase its collaboration with the Government to strengthen India’s VFX capabilities and nurture a future-ready talent pipeline. Its participation will also feature the Gala Premiere of Pushpak Viman, an international screening of Ray Gunn and engagement in pitching sessions to support emerging creative talent and foster industry opportunities.
Masterclasses, Panels & Interactive Programmes
IFFI 2026 will host 14 sessions at Kala Academy from 21 to 27 November 2026, featuring masterclasses, workshops, panel discussions, retrospectives, in-conversation and interview sessions.
The sessions will bring together filmmakers, artists and industry professionals to explore subjects ranging from documentary cinema and filmmaking across borders to women shaping world cinema, storytelling, casting, subtitling and emerging cinematic practices.
Centenary Tributes & Restored Classics
The festival will celebrate the legacy of distinguished filmmakers and artists through centenary tributes, retrospectives and restored classics.
A special centenary tribute to filmmaker
Andrzej Wajda
will feature five films. The Restored Classics section will also present five films, providing audiences an opportunity to revisit significant works of cinematic history.
Festival Venues & Public Engagement
The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) is set to transform Goa into a vibrant cinematic destination, with nine days of film screenings across 13 indoor screens at four locations. From the bustling festival hub of Panaji, with seven screens across INOX, Maquinez, Samrat and Ashoka, to the INOX screens at Porvorim, and the iconic Ravindra Bhavan in Margao and Magic Movie in Ponda, the festival promises an immersive cinematic experience for film enthusiasts. With diverse screening spaces and a combined seating capacity of over 4,000, IFFI will bring the magic of world cinema closer to audiences across Goa.
Centenary Celebrations
IFFI 2026 will celebrate the birth centenaries of eminent personalities of Indian cinema, paying tribute to legendary filmmakers Shakti Samanta and Raj Khosla, actors Uttam Kumar, Suryakant Mandhare, Prem Nazir and Raj Kumar, and renowned music composers O. P. Nayyar and Ravi. The festival will honour their exceptional contributions to Indian cinema and their enduring legacy in shaping the country’s cinematic and musical heritage.
The 57th IFFI concludes with Anthony Chen’s We Are All Strangers
The closing film of the 57th IFFI, We Are All Strangers, directed by Anthony Chen, represents Singapore and has a runtime of 157 minutes. Presented in Mandarin and English, the film brings the festival to a close with a distinctive cinematic offering from contemporary Singaporean cinema.

About International Film Festival of India (IFFI)
Established in 1952, the International Film Festival of India is one of Asia’s oldest and prominent international film festivals. Organised by the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, Government of India, in association with the Government of Goa and the Entertainment Society of Goa, IFFI celebrates the best of world cinema while promoting Indian films and talent on a global platform. Held annually in Goa, the festival serves as a platform for creative exchange, discovery of new voices and fostering cultural understanding through cinema.

The National Film Development Corporation of India is a public sector enterprise under the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting. title: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Takes Swachhata Beyond Office Walls as Special Campaign 6.0 Concludes
subtitle: Clean neighbourhoods, innovative e-waste reuse and greener workplaces mark the campaign
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 8:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), along with its organisations, undertook a series of initiatives during Special Campaign 6.0 (2–31 October 2026), focusing on cleanliness, pendency reduction, record management and environmental sustainability across its offices and field establishments.
The campaign covered 142 locations, resulting in the reclamation of 1,500 sq. ft. of space and generation of ₹2,47,156 through the disposal of scrap and obsolete items, including e-waste. Beyond office premises, the campaign also promoted cleanliness in public spaces, community participation and innovative approaches to e-waste reuse. The campaign also recorded significant progress in reducing pendency and improving record management, with the following key outcomes:
Campaign Scorecard
The Ministry undertook cleanliness drives at 142 locations, resulting in the reclamation of 1,500 sq. ft. of office space and generation of revenue amounting to ₹2,47,156 through the disposal of scrap and obsolete items, including e-waste. Significant achievements were also recorded in pendency reduction and records management, including:
Disposal of 11 PMO references, 29 references received from Members of Parliament and 2 Parliamentary Assurances.
Redressal of 1,973 public grievances and 84 grievance appeals.
Review of 2,924 physical files, of which 233 files were weeded out.
Review of 355 e-files, of which 87 e-files were closed.
Swachhata Pledge and Public Participation
The campaign commenced with a Swachhata pledge administered to around 250 officials of the Ministry and its field offices, building on the momentum of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 (17th September–2nd October). Citizens were also encouraged to take the online pledge through the Ministry's website:
https://dashboard.msme.gov.in/events/pledge.aspx
.
Cleaning the Neighbourhood: Swachhata Beyond Office Premises
Extending cleanliness drives to public spaces, NSIC's Head Office team, along with Safai Mitras, undertook cleaning activities at nearby public places including metro stations, parks etc. Shopkeepers, students and residents were sensitised about waste segregation and keeping public spaces clean.
At Rajajinagar Industrial Area, Bengaluru, NSIC's Branch Office and local volunteers cleared litter, cleaned public walkways and segregated biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste. Neighbouring industrialists were also sensitised about sustainable waste management.
Before: litter heap at Rajajinagar, Bengaluru
After: the same stretch, cleared
Similarly, MGIRI organised a cleanliness drive at the river ghat in Yelakeli village, Wardha district, Maharashtra, on 13th October 2026.
Before Dirty river ghat Wardha, Maharashtra
After: the same ghat, cleaned
From E-Waste to a Working Charkha
MGIRI, Wardha, demonstrated the potential of e-waste reuse by developing a functional Charkha almost entirely from discarded electronic components. Motherboards, PCB strips, pulleys from old DVD drives, bearings and other discarded components were repurposed to create the working model. The initiative exemplifies the principles of Reduce, Reuse and Recycle, showcasing innovation in converting electronic waste into useful products.
Greener and More Welcoming Workplaces
The Ministry introduced greenery across its office workspaces by placing potted plants along workstation partitions, creating a fresher and more welcoming environment.
Potted plants along the workstations, M/o MSME office
NSIC’s Branch Office at Naini developed a Swachhata Selfie Point by creatively shaping its garden lawn into the letters “N S I C”. The initiative was executed in-house at zero cost, without the use of plastic or flex materials, presenting a simple, sustainable and replicable model for other offices. Additionally, NSIC Head Office enhanced its reception areas by incorporating greenery, further promoting a clean, green and welcoming workplace environment.
Taking Swachhata to Villages, Schools and Communities
Citizen engagement remained an important component of the campaign. On 6th October, MGIRI organised a Swachhata and hygiene awareness programme involving staff and villagers at Go-Vigyan Anusandhan Kendra, Devlapar.
Similarly, KVIC engaged with students and local communities through awareness programmes. On 5th October, it organised a seminar, debate and essay competition for over 100 students at Nandkishore Kailash Chandra Mahavidyalaya, Sitapur, Uttar Pradesh, along with Charkha and pottery-wheel demonstrations. Swachhata pledges were also administered at schools and colleges, during a PMEGP awareness camp in Ooty and at Mohamed Sathak College, Ramanathapuram, Tamil Nadu.
Pledge in a school assembly
Awareness and Capacity Building
Standees and banners were displayed across offices to spread awareness about the campaign among officials and visitors. Ministry officials were also encouraged to undertake identified courses on e-waste management and record management through the i-GOT Karmayogi platform.
Sustaining the Momentum
Special Campaign 6.0 reaffirmed the significance of collective participation in promoting cleanliness, sustainability and environmental responsibility. The Ministry of MSME remains committed to institutionalising these initiatives through regular cleanliness drives, expeditious disposal of pending matters, effective records management and scientific disposal of e-waste. These sustained efforts aim to foster cleaner, greener and more efficient workplaces across the MSME ecosystem.

content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, Dr. Jitendra Singh, held a bilateral meeting with Italy's Minister of University and Research, Ms. Anna Maria Bernini, to strengthen the longstanding India-Italy scientific partnership and take forward joint research and innovation initiatives under the bilateral Science & Technology cooperation framework.
The discussions focused on translating the India-Italy Strategic Partnership into practical scientific collaboration, strengthening institutional mechanisms and exploring new opportunities for joint research in emerging and priority technology areas.
Highlighting the longstanding foundation of bilateral scientific cooperation, Dr. Jitendra Singh noted that the first Inter-governmental Agreement in Science & Technology between India and Italy was signed in 1978 and subsequently renewed on November 28, 2003.
The agreement envisages sharing experiences in national research, development and innovation policies and programmes, exchange of scientists and researchers, industrial research, joint research and development projects and joint workshops.
India-Italy relations were elevated to a Strategic Partnership in 2023. Subsequently, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and Italian Prime Minister Ms. Giorgia Meloni announced the Joint Strategic Action Plan (JSAP) for 2025-2029 in November 2024, providing a roadmap for strengthening bilateral cooperation.
As a follow-up to the Joint Strategic Action Plan, an Italian delegation led by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Mr. Antonio Tajani, along with Minister of University and Research Ms. Anna Maria Bernini, visited New Delhi in April 2025. During the visit, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between India's Ministry of Science and Technology and Italy's Ministry of University and Research (MUR), marking an important step towards strengthening bilateral scientific cooperation.
Under the framework of the Science & Technology Agreement, the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Italy have been supporting bilateral scientific and technological activities through the Indo-Italian Executive Programme of Cooperation (EPOC). More than 150 joint projects have been implemented under the programme.
The current EPOC for the period 2025-27 was signed on April 10, 2025, during the Joint Science & Technology Committee meeting. Under this programme, both sides agreed to jointly fund 10 proposals for Mobility of Researchers and 10 proposals for Significant Research, providing opportunities for researchers from the two countries to undertake collaborative scientific activities.
The first India-Italy Science and Innovation Dialogue was held in New Delhi on April 11, 2025, alongside the bilateral engagements. Experts from research centres and academic institutions participated in the dialogue and exchanged ideas on future areas of collaboration.
The Second India-Italy Science and Innovation Dialogue 2026 is being organised as a continuation of this engagement. The Indian delegation comprises experts and representatives from academic institutions, research institutes, incubators and technology incubation hubs. The participation of these diverse stakeholders reflects the importance of connecting research, academia and the innovation ecosystem in advancing bilateral scientific cooperation.
Dr. Jitendra Singh acknowledged the ongoing efforts by both sides to translate the shared cooperation framework into concrete joint initiatives. He particularly highlighted the role of the India-Italy Joint Scientific Council (IIJSC), which is responsible for the implementation and pursuit of cooperation activities under the Memorandum of Understanding.
Looking ahead, both sides are in the process of launching a new call in 2027 under the broader framework of the MoU. The proposed areas of research cooperation include Artificial Intelligence, High-Performance Computing and Big Data; Clean Technologies, Hydrogen, Renewable Energy and the Energy Transition; and Advanced Biotechnology and Biomedical Research, with particular attention to gene therapy, mRNA technologies and biomanufacturing.
These thematic areas reflect the broad scope for advancing collaborative research and innovation by bringing together the scientific and technological capabilities of both countries.
Dr. Jitendra Singh expressed the hope that India and Italy would maintain their close association to promote practical cooperation by leveraging the Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) ecosystems of both countries. He assured full cooperation from the Indian side for the delivery of mutually agreed projects and programmes.
The bilateral meeting and the Second India-Italy Science and Innovation Dialogue form part of Dr. Jitendra Singh's official visit to Italy from November 11 to 15, 2026, aimed at further strengthening the scientific and technological dimension of the India-Italy Strategic Partnership.

Through the NAMASTE Scheme, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to promote safer working conditions, social security and dignified livelihoods, contributing to a more inclusive, sustainable and mechanised sanitation ecosystem.
Ensuring safe working conditions, occupational health and dignified livelihoods for sanitation workers, is an important step towards building an inclusive and sustainable sanitation ecosystem.
The National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment seeks to strengthen the safety, dignity and socio-economic well-being of sanitation workers through access to protective equipment, safety training and institutional support.
For several years, Mr. Ramasamy worked as a sewer and septic tank cleaner, often without adequate personal protective equipment (PPE), exposing himself to occupational hazards and associated health risks.
Prolonged exposure to hazardous working conditions resulted in recurring skin infections, injuries and physical discomfort. These health concerns frequently disrupted his work attendance, leading to loss of wages and financial difficulties. Alongside occupational health challenges, he also experienced the social stigma associated with sanitation work.
With a family of four dependent on his earnings, maintaining household stability while managing health-related expenses remained a significant challenge. Despite these difficulties, Ramasamy aspired to work in safer conditions, secure a stable livelihood and provide better opportunities for his children.
A significant turning point came in 2025 when he received assistance under the NAMASTE Scheme. As part of the intervention, he was provided with a comprehensive PPE kit comprising protective overalls, gloves, safety boots, a face mask and a safety helmet. He also underwent structured training on safe sewage handling practices, occupational safety, hazard prevention and the proper use of protective equipment. In addition, he was linked with social security support to strengthen his overall well-being.
The intervention enabled Ramasamy to adopt safer working practices and develop greater awareness of occupational hazards. Access to appropriate protective equipment contributed to a reduction in recurring skin infections and work-related injuries, improving his health and enabling more regular attendance at work.
The improvement in his working conditions also contributed to greater financial stability. His monthly income increased from approximately ₹8,000 to around ₹12,000, registering a 50 per cent rise. Improved work attendance and fewer health-related disruptions enabled him to contribute more consistently towards household expenses and the needs of his family.
With improved occupational safety, greater financial security and increased awareness of safe sanitation practices, Ramasamy has experienced a positive transformation in his professional and personal life. The support received under NAMASTE has helped him continue his work with greater confidence while strengthening his ability to provide for his family.

‘Creating a Well-Functioning Care Economy’,
SHATAYU has been developed as a centralised national Geriatric Caregiver Dashboard and Directory. The platform seeks to bridge the gap between professionally trained geriatric caregivers and senior citizens, their families and institutions requiring specialised elderly care services.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said with India’s elderly population steadily increasing, the need for a structured, skilled and accessible geriatric care workforce is becoming increasingly important. He said SHATAYU represents an important step towards addressing this requirement by bringing together trained caregivers, families and institutions through a common digital platform. By facilitating access to caregiving professionals while creating organised employment pathways for skilled individuals, the initiative seeks to strengthen India’s care economy and promote a more inclusive, accessible and responsive support system for senior citizens, he said.
The Ministry Official said the SHATAYU portal currently features 30,151 caregivers in its national directory, providing a digital database of caregiving professionals across States and Union Territories. Through this directory, individuals and families can search for caregivers based on geographical location, including State/UT and district, making it easier to identify locally available caregiving support, he said.
The Official said to promote transparency and accountability, SHATAYU incorporates digital facilities such as OTP-based verification for callback requests, caregiver profile access, enrolment tracking and a feedback and rating mechanism. These features facilitate communication between caregivers and service seekers and provide an avenue for users to share their experience of caregiving services.
He said SHATAYU provides a direct digital interface connecting citizens with trained geriatric caregivers. Through its caregiver directory, individuals and families can explore caregiver profiles and identify professionals according to their requirements, he said.
The platform also offers a convenient “Request Callback” facility for individuals seeking assistance in engaging a caregiver, the Official said adding the users can select their preferred State/UT and district, specify the type of care required and submit their contact details through an OTP-based verification process.
The request is subsequently made available to caregivers in the selected district, facilitating direct communication between service seekers and caregiving professionals, the Official said.
The facility caters to both full-time and hourly caregiving requirements, while searching the directory and placing callback requests are available free of charge, he added.
The SHATAYU portal can be accessed at
https://shatayu.dosje.gov.in/
The Official said recognising that the care requirements of senior citizens vary according to their health conditions and individual needs, the platform facilitates access to specialised caregiving services.
These include general geriatric care, post-surgical care, dementia and Alzheimer’s care, physiotherapy and mobility assistance, palliative care and other elderly care requirements, he said.
The Official said the integrated approach enables families to explore suitable caregiving support for elderly members, including those requiring assistance with daily activities, rehabilitation and specialised care.
Beyond facilitating access to elderly care, SHATAYU also aims to strengthen the professional geriatric care workforce by providing visibility and employment opportunities to trained caregivers, the Official further said.
The Ministry Official informed the platform enables eligible professionals to enrol themselves by submitting their personal details, address information, course qualifications and training certificates. Applicants can also track their enrolment status through the dashboard, he said adding that following the review and approval of applications, eligible caregiver profiles are listed on the platform, enabling prospective employers and families to connect with them.
The initiative recognises four broad professional training categories, namely Geriatric Care Provider, Geriatric Caregiver (Institutional and Home Care), Wellness Therapist (Elderly) and Elderly Care Companion, the Official said. These training tracks encompass a range of competencies, including holistic elderly care, physiological monitoring, emergency handling, bedside mobility, assistance with daily living activities, therapeutic rehabilitation, cognitive engagement, emotional companionship and social integration, the Official added.
The Ministyry Official informed the training framework is supported by the National Institute of Social Defence (NISD) and the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), under the respective Ministries of Social Justice and Empowerment and Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.
Through SHATAYU, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to advance its commitment towards ensuring dignity, well-being, independence and quality care for senior citizens, while supporting the development of a skilled and professionally recognised geriatric care workforce.

title: Inviting feedback and suggestions on the Report submitted by Committee on Knowledge Systems
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 2:40PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The development of a systematic framework to measure the contribution of knowledge and knowledge products to the Indian economy assumes significance in the context of the growing role of knowledge in driving economic activity, productivity and value creation. Towards this, a series of deliberations were initiated with a meeting chaired by Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India on 10 February 2025, which provided the initial direction for the exercise. Subsequently, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) constituted a Technical Advisory Group (TAG) in May 2025 under the chairmanship of Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, the then Member, Capacity Building Commission, to guide the development of a measurement framework. As part of its deliberations, the TAG held a brainstorming workshop on 30 September 2025, organised by MoSPI. The suggestions and insights emerging from the workshop, along with those from subsequent expert consultations, guided the preparation of the Base Paper on the
Framework for Measuring the Contribution of Knowledge and Knowledge Products to the Indian Economy
released in May 2026.
Building on this foundation, MoSPI constituted a Committee on Knowledge Systems on 5 May 2026 under the chairmanship of Shri Ratan P. Watal, former Member Secretary of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, with the mandate to prepare an Actionable Policy Paper on the Framework for Measuring the Contribution of Knowledge and Knowledge Products to the Economy.
The said Committee undertook a broader examination of the subject, drawing upon diverse perspectives and evidence, to develop an actionable framework for measuring their contribution to the Indian economy. The Committee has submitted to the Ministry its final report, which contains the
Actionable Policy Paper on Framework for Measuring the Contribution of Knowledge and Knowledge Products to the Economy
.
The report can be accessed
here
(https://www.mospi.gov.in/announcements).
The Actionable Policy Paper sets out the background and context for this exercise. India’s development aspirations under the Viksit Bharat vision call for sustained improvements in productivity, innovation and the capacity to create economic value. Strengthening the knowledge base, know-how and specialised capabilities required to generate, acquire, absorb, adapt and apply knowledge will increasingly shape the country’s development trajectory. Understanding the contribution of knowledge to the economy is therefore essential for identifying existing strengths, recognising capability gaps and setting priorities to guide India’s future development. This task is becoming increasingly complex as the nature and processes of knowledge creation themselves evolve rapidly, with powerful AI systems generating knowledge and developing solutions in ways that extend beyond conventional models of human knowledge creation.
The Paper establishes the rationale for systematically measuring productive knowledge as a driver of economic growth, productivity, competitiveness and strategic capabilities. It outlines the Knowledge Ecosystem with eight interrelated components: knowledge, capabilities and assets, enabling infrastructure, knowledge creation activities, knowledge products, knowledge-embedded products, knowledge-intensive entrepreneurship and knowledge application. It also proposes boundary conditions for identifying knowledge products: knowledge as input, knowledge content, identifiability, codification and economic value. It has been also stated that these boundaries only serve as broad guiding principles rather than rigid criteria, while leaving sufficient flexibility to accommodate the diversity and evolving nature of such products.
Cross-country experience shows that knowledge-related activity and products are typically captured through multiple complementary accounts. Similar efforts are also underway in India to develop a more comprehensive understanding of emerging and knowledge-intensive areas of economic activity. These include the initiation of work on a Culture Satellite Account in 2025, ongoing work to develop a framework for measuring the contribution of the Space Economy to GDP, and a study conducted in 2025 to estimate the contribution of Digital Economy to the GDP for the year 2022–23.
In view of the above, and since comprehensively measuring the knowledge ecosystem simultaneously is infeasible, the Paper recommends that a family of SNA 2025-consistent thematic statistics/accounts may be developed instead of a single aggregate measure for the entire Knowledge Ecosystem in order to facilitate policy-making.  Priorities may be assigned among the major components and sub-components of the ecosystem, based on their contributions to growth, productivity, competitiveness, inclusive growth and livelihoods, future significance and cost-effective measurability. It further recommends to consider developing thematic statistics/accounts in areas like Human Capital, R&D, Creative Economy, AI systems, Data and Databases, High-Tech Products and Frontier Technologies and Digital Economy on a priority basis.
To help build thematic statistics/accounts, the Paper proposes a federated model that distributes responsibilities according to each institution’s mandate and comparative strengths. It would involve three roles: system integrators, which provide the common measurement framework; domain institutions, including sectoral ministries and departments, which measure specialised components; and key partners, including State Governments, regulatory institutions and research and academic institutions.
Feedback and suggestions on the Actionable Policy Paper are invited from all stakeholders and the general public as part of the consultation process. Feedback may be shared with this Ministry on the email ID:
rau-2@mospi.gov.in
by 12 December 2026.

title: The Manufacturing Transformation Powered by PLI
subtitle: From Policy to Production
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 5:36PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) framework has emerged as one of India's most significant industrial policy interventions. Spanning
14 strategic sectors
, the scheme has attracted investments, expanded manufacturing capacity, boosted exports and generated employment across the country. More importantly, it has helped strengthen domestic value chains and position India as a competitive manufacturing destination. As India advances towards Viksit Bharat 2047, PLI is laying the foundations for a more resilient, innovative and globally integrated industrial economy.
The Moment India Decided to Build
A smartphone assembled in Tamil Nadu. A solar module manufactured in Gujarat. A pharmaceutical ingredient produced in a bulk drug park. These are not isolated milestones. They are proof points of India's emergence as a
more self-reliant
,
technology-driven
and
globally integrated economy
. In sectors such as electronics, electric mobility and renewable energy, the focus is shifting from building capacity to building ecosystems.
At the heart of this shift lies the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme, introduced in 2020. Over the past six years, it has catalysed investments across sectors - translating policy ambition into production capacity. As India advances towards
Viksit Bharat 2047
, the next phase depends on deepening value chains and strengthening India's role in global production networks.
From Policy to Production: The Rise of the PLI Framework
Launched under Atmanirbhar Bharat, the PLI scheme
was designed to
accelerate manufacturing growth.
Initially, it encompassed sectors such as mobile manufacturing, specific electronic components, active pharmaceutical ingredients, and medical devices. However, as the scheme evolved, it expanded to encompass a total of
14 strategic sectors
, including pharmaceuticals, textiles, specialty steel, etc.,
with a total approved financial outlay of ₹1.91 lakh crore (₹1,91,049 crore).
At its core lies a simple idea- when domestic industries grow in scale, quality and competitiveness, investment, exports, jobs and innovation grow alongside them.
The Numbers Behind the Transformation
India’s manufacturing and export performance is gaining momentum across several PLI-supported sectors. During 2021- 2025, several PLI sectors recorded strong export growth, including
IT Hardware (77.2%)
,
ACC Batteries (45.0%)
,
Electronics (38.8%)
,
Solar PV Modules (23.9%)
, and
Specialty Steel (22.5%)
on an average annual basis.
As of
30 June 2026
, approved applications stood at
791 across 14 sectors
, with cumulative actual
investment
exceeding
₹2.58 lakh crore (₹2,58,835 crore)
and cumulative
production/sales crossing ₹23.79 lakh crore
. Exports were
boosted by ₹15.53 lakh crore
, while
over 14.57 lakh direct and indirect jobs
were generated (comprising 8.81 lakh direct jobs and 5.75 lakh indirect jobs across IT Hardware, LSEM, and Solar PV Modules). Cumulative incentive disbursement reached ₹36,754 crore. The level of incentive disbursement reflects the performance-linked nature of the scheme. Incentives are released when companies meet the required investment, production and other eligibility criteria. As projects move forward and begin production, eligible claims are made in line with the provisions of the respective schemes.
Sectoral outcomes show deeper localisation, with mobile imports declining nearly 77%.
PLI also enabled first-time domestic manufacturing of 191 bulk drugs, while telecom exports reached ₹21,033 crore.
These trends reflect how domestic manufacturing is increasingly integrating with global value chains.
Building the New Industrial India
Across sectors, the PLI framework is translating policy into tangible outcomes. New factories, expanded production lines and emerging industrial clusters are reshaping India's manufacturing landscape. Policy support is translating into tangible outcomes, creating new opportunities for industry, workers and entrepreneurs alike. Some of the sectors with clear outcomes are:
Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing (LSEM): Powering India's Digital Manufacturing Rise
The electronics manufacturing and IT hardware sector has been the largest beneficiary of the PLI scheme.
With the LSEM scheme tenure now completed, companies under the scheme achieved a cumulative investment of ₹20,580.20 crore
(nearly three times the initial target of ₹7,000 crore),
cumulative production of ₹11,61,505 crore, direct employment of 1,69,249, and cumulative incentive disbursement of ₹19,090.98 crore till June 2026
(alongside ₹954 crore investment, ₹24,386 crore production, 5,216 direct jobs, and ₹97.84
crore disbursed under IT Hardware 2.0).
Electronics production
rose
from ₹11.32 lakh crore
in
2024-25
to
₹13.11 lakh crore
in
2025-26
, a
15.8% year-on-year increase
.
This growth reflects a significant shift in India’s electronics manufacturing capabilities. Compared with 2014-15, electronics
production
is now
seven times higher
. Electronics
exports
have increased
eleven-fold
to
₹4.24 lakh crore
, strengthening India’s global market presence.  Mobile manufacturing has emerged as a key driver of this transformation. Mobile phone production has risen
33 times
to
₹6.27 lakh crore
. India today is the
second largest mobile manufacturer
in volume terms. The country has transitioned from being a net importer of mobile phones in 2014 to becoming a net exporter of mobile phones. Further,
99.2%
of mobile phones used in India are now
made domestically
.
Pharmaceuticals: Strengthening the Pharmacy of the World
India is the
world's 3rd largest
pharmaceutical industry
by volume
and
11th largest by value
. The country supplies nearly
20% of the world’s generic medicines
and serves a significant share of pharmaceutical demand across key markets.
PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals has a
financial outlay of ₹15,000 crore for 2020- 21 to 2028- 29
. The scheme supports domestic manufacturing of high-value pharmaceutical products and technological upgradation.
Reflecting strong industry confidence,
as on 30 June 2026, the scheme has recorded cumulative investments of ₹46,744 crore, cumulative production/sales of ₹4,02,869 crore (over ₹4.02 lakh crore), direct employment of 1,21,294, and cumulative incentive disbursement of ₹6,662 crore
, supporting investments in advanced manufacturing, product diversification, and export-oriented growth. Additionally, under the Bulk Drugs PLI scheme (outlay of ₹6,940 crore), cumulative investment reached ₹5,211 crore, sales ₹3,792 crore, direct jobs 5,127, and incentives ₹88 crore; while under the Medical Devices PLI scheme (outlay of ₹3,420 crore), investment reached ₹1,185 crore, sales ₹16,612 crore, direct jobs 5,769, and incentives ₹266.64 crore.
Telecom & Networking Products: Advancing Import Substitution
The telecom sector emerged as one of the early success stories under the PLI framework
with a financial outlay of ₹12,195 crore
. During 2021-25,
telecom exports
recorded an average
annual growth of 1.5 per cent
, while imports declined by 18.5 per cent annually.
As of 30 June 2026, the scheme has attracted cumulative investments of ₹5,627 crore, achieved cumulative production/sales of ₹1,20,721 crore, created 36,319 direct jobs, and disbursed ₹2,796 crore in incentives.
This trend indicates an early accomplishment in import substitution, aligning with the PLI framework's overarching objective of enhancing market penetration abroad.
White Goods (ACs and LED Lights): Building the Parts That Matter
Behind every air conditioner and LED light lies a network of high-value components that determine both cost and competitiveness. Through the PLI Scheme for White Goods
(with a financial outlay of ₹6,238 crore)
, India is steadily building these capabilities at home. Reflecting the sector's growing momentum, budgetary support increased from
₹303.54 crore in 2025-26 (Revised Estimate)
to
₹1,003.54 crore in 2026-27 (Budget Estimate)
. The fourth round of the scheme attracted
13 applications with committed investments of ₹1,914 crore.
The applications were received during the window from 15 September to 10 November 2025, with strong participation from MSMEs.
As of 30 June 2026, the scheme has achieved cumulative investments of ₹7,670 crore, cumulative production/sales of ₹57,057 crore, direct employment of 54,049, and cumulative incentive disbursement of ₹593 crore.
Automobile & Auto Components Industry: Driving the Mobility Revolution
The PLI Scheme for Automobiles and Auto Components is accelerating India’s transition towards advanced and sustainable mobility. With an
outlay of ₹25,938 crore
, the scheme is supporting development of electric vehicles, advanced automotive technologies and high-value components, while strengthening India’s position in the global automotive value chain.
The government’s continued commitment is reflected in the
increase in budgetary support, from ₹2,091.26 crore in 2025-26 (RE)
to
₹5,939.87 crore in 2026-27 (BE)
.
As of 30 June 2026, the scheme has attracted cumulative investments of ₹45,477 crore, recorded cumulative production/sales of ₹64,374 crore, generated direct employment of 71,337, and disbursed ₹3,174.15 crore in incentives.
Food Processing Industry: From Farm Gates to Global Markets
The food processing sector is combining manufacturing growth with rural value creation. With an outlay
of ₹10,900 crore
,
PLI Scheme for the Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI)
is being implemented from 2021-22 to 2026-27.
As of 30 June 2026, around 3.36 lakh (3,35,516) direct and indirect jobs
have been created, far surpassing the scheme’s target of
2.5 lakh jobs by 2026-27
.
Some key achievements under the PLISFPI scheme include:
165 approved applications
across multiple food processing categories.
69 MSMEs
among the approved beneficiaries.
274 project locations
established across the country, contributing to regional industrial development.
₹9,207 crore
worth of cumulative investments reported by beneficiary companies,
with cumulative production/sales reaching ₹5,13,104 crore (over ₹5.13 lakh crore) as of 30 June 2026.
₹3,271.44 crore
in cumulative incentives disbursed
as of 30 June 2026 (including ₹1,193 crore in 2025-26 and ₹556.64 crore in 2026-27 till June 2026).
Building on this momentum, a dedicated
PLI Scheme for Millet-Based Products (PLISMBP)
was introduced in 2022-23 from savings under PLISFPI. As on June 2026, out of total allocation of ₹800 crores for PLISMBP, an amount of
₹793.27crore
has been approved to incentivise 29 applicants, which includes
8 large and 21 Small & Medium entities
.
Specialty Steel: Strengthening India’s Industrial Backbone
From infrastructure and automobiles to defence and engineering, specialty steel forms the backbone of several strategic industries.
Specialty steel
is the downstream, value-added product of steel manufacturing process. To strengthen domestic capabilities, the Government launched the
PLI Scheme for Specialty Steel in 2021
with a
financial outlay of ₹6,322 crore
. As of
30 June 2026
, the scheme had
attracted ₹27,368 crore
in
cumulative investments
, achieved
cumulative production/sales of ₹4,170 crore
,
created 16,200 direct jobs
and
disbursed ₹236 crore in incentives
.
Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage: Powering the Clean Energy Future
India is rapidly shifting towards electric mobility and clean energy. In this context, domestic battery manufacturing has emerged as a strategic priority. The
PLI Scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage
was approved in May 2021 with an outlay of ₹18,100 crore. It targets
50 GWh of domestic ACC manufacturing capacity and an additional cumulative capacity of (5) GWh for Niche ACC Technologies
. Of this,
40 GWh was awarded to four beneficiary firms in two rounds by August 2025
, while a 10 GWh capacity for grid-scale stationary storage is being tendered separately in 2026. The scheme is for strengthening domestic manufacturing and reducing dependence on imported ACCs.
As of 30 June 2026, it had attracted ₹5,270 crore in cumulative investment and generated 1,292 direct jobs.
High Efficiency Solar PV: Building India's Solar Manufacturing Engine
Solar energy sits at the heart of India's clean energy ambitions, demanding a strong domestic manufacturing base. The PLI Scheme for High-Efficiency Solar PV Modules, with an
outlay of ₹24,000 crore
, addresses this directly. The scheme promotes domestic manufacturing, reduces import dependence, and encourages value addition across the solar value chain. Under the scheme, letters of award have been issued for setting up
48,337 MW
of fully/partially integrated solar PV module manufacturing capacity. By September 2025, the scheme had attracted investments of around
₹52,900 crore
. It had also generated direct employment for about
44,400 people
.
The Journey from Policy to Prosperity
What began as a policy experiment in 2020 has become a defining chapter in India's industrial history. PLI has done more than incentivise production- it has shifted the national mindset.
Manufacturing is no longer a background activity but a strategic priority.
The real measure of PLI's success is not just in the numbers. It lies in the factories that didn't exist six years ago, the engineers now working on EV batteries, the farmers whose produce reaches global shelves. India is not just making more- it is making differently.
As the next phase begins, the ambition is clear: not just to produce for the world, but to innovate for it.

title: India’s Renewable Energy Journey: Powering a Cleaner Future
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 1:02PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India’s Energy Landscape
India’s renewable energy landscape is expanding rapidly to meet rising demand, strengthen energy security, and support a cleaner future. The transformation spans solar, wind, hydro, bio-energy, geothermal and green hydrogen.
Policy support, infrastructure development, domestic production, manufacturing expansion and wider energy access are shaping this transformation. From rooftop solar for households to large wind, floating solar and storage projects, India is steadily raising the share of renewables in its energy mix.
Numbers At a Glance:
Total installed power capacity:
Around
560 GW
in October 2026, up from 249 GW in 2014.
Non-fossil capacity: 308 GW
as of 31 July 2026, accounting for
55%
of total installed capacity.
India ranks third
globally in
renewable energy
installed capacity.
India invested
USD 63.7 billion
in its renewable energy sector during July 2024–June 2026.
Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRESE) 2026
Invest. Innovate. Inspire
The
Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRESE) 2026
was held from 2–5 November in New Delhi. The Summit brought together
global policymakers, investors, industry leaders, manufacturers and innovators
. Australia, Denmark, the European Union, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom participated as country partners. Thirteen Indian States and Union Territories, including Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh, showcased their renewable energy potential, investment opportunities and manufacturing capabilities. The event also featured an exhibition bringing together 400+ manufacturers, technology providers, startups and research institutions. Discussions covered
renewable energy financing, clean energy manufacturing, energy storage, emerging technologies and workforce development
.
Solar Power: Scaling Up, Reaching More People
India’s
installed solar capacity
has reached
~175 GW
(as of 31 October 2026), rising from 2.8 GW in 2014. Solar is now the largest component of India’s renewable energy capacity.
India became the world’s second-largest solar growth market in 2025
, adding more than
37 GW
of solar capacity, compared with
34 GW
added by the United States.
PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
Launched with a total outlay of ₹75,021 crore for 1 crore households in February 2024.
65.26 lakh households
are now benefiting from rooftop solar installations across the country (As of 02.11.2026).
Approximately
₹35,800 crore in subsidy
has been transferred to the beneficiaries.
Nearly
21 lakh households
have received zero electricity bills till October, 2026.
Cumulatively,
19.1 GW of rooftop solar capacity has been commissioned
under the scheme so far.
Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana
The government approved the
Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY)
on
31 July 2026
with an outlay of
₹5,070 crore
. It adds a new dimension to India's solar expansion with the development of
Floating Solar Photovoltaic Projects with Energy Storage Systems.
Target:
5,000 MW of Floating Solar PV projects.
Co-located storage with a minimum two-hour duration, equivalent to
10,000 MWh.
Projects to be sanctioned from
FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31.
Wind Energy
Wind energy continues to be an important pillar of India’s renewable energy expansion. India ranks
fourth globally in installed wind power capacity
. The sector is also seeing stronger annual additions and growing domestic manufacturing.
Installed capacity: 59.20 GW as on 29 October 2026
.
India added
6.05 GW in FY 2025–26
, its highest-ever annual wind capacity addition and
46% higher
than FY 2024–25.
Around
28 GW
of additional wind capacity is under implementation.
Wind turbine manufacturing capacity reached about
24 GW
(March 2026), up from 10 GW in 2014. The sector has achieved
70–80% indigenisation
across key components.
The Union Cabinet approved a
₹7,453 crore VGF scheme
on 19 June 2024 for
1 GW of offshore wind projects
.
Bio-Energy
Bio-power capacity stands at 11.75 GW as of 29 October 2026. The CBG ecosystem has also expanded, with 839 CBG plants registered as of 02 November 2026. Of these, 210 have been commissioned and 255 are under construction.
Biomass cogeneration: 9821.32 MW
of bagasse-based and
1047.85 MW
of non-bagasse capacity as of
30 September 2026
.
Waste-to-Energy:
As of 30 September 2026, grid-connected waste-to-energy capacity stood at 324.24 MW. Off-grid plants contributed another 554.16 MW.
National Bioenergy Programme:
The programme supports
Waste-to-Energy, Biomass and Biogas projects
through financial assistance. Phase-I covered
FY 2021–22 to FY 2025–26,
with an outlay of
₹858 crore.
GOBARdhan: Turning Waste into Energy Growth
Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan (GOBARdhan)– National Circular Bioenergy Scheme:
Approved by the government on
6 August 2026
, with an outlay of
₹23,731 crore
for
FY 2026–27 to FY 2035–36
.
The scheme aims to
nearly ten-fold domestic CBG production
and create a national circular bioeconomy.
Llar Cooperation
Hydro
Hydropower remains an important source of renewable electricity, providing reliable and flexible power generation. It also supports grid stability as solar and wind capacity expand. Cumulative capacity of
hydro power
is
57.49 GW (as of 29 October 2026)
, including large and small hydro.
Small Hydro Power Development Scheme
The government has approved the
Small Hydro Power (SHP) Development Scheme
in March 2026 for
FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31
, with an outlay of
₹2,584.60 crore
.
The scheme aims to add approximately
1,500 MW
of small hydro capacity through projects of
1–25 MW
. It particularly supports projects in
hilly and North-Eastern regions
.
Green Hydrogen
Green hydrogen has emerged as a clean fuel option for hard-to-abate sectors. It can also support energy security and industrial growth.
National Green Hydrogen Mission:
The government launched
the National Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM)
in 2023 as an umbrella programme to establish a Green Hydrogen ecosystem and catalyse a systemic response to the opportunities and challenges in this sector.
Approved in January 2023 with an outlay of
₹19,744 crore
, targeting
5 MMT (Million Metric Tonne)
of green hydrogen production by 2030.
Indian companies have signed
5.5 lakh MTPA
of Green Hydrogen offtake commitments since 2023, the world’s largest supply commitment.
Indian companies signed 18 new offtake agreements in 2026, covering
over 4 lakh MTPA
of Green Hydrogen equivalent.
Over 70%
of the total 5.5 lakh MTPA offtake commitments since 2023 are earmarked for exports.
Green Hydrogen projects are expected to attract investments of around
₹90,000 crore
(US$9.5 billion).
Production capacity:
Around
8,000 tonnes per annum
of green hydrogen production capacity had been commissioned by
February 2026
.
Transport:
In July 2026, the Government launched
12 pilot projects
under the Mission for
70 hydrogen-powered vehicles across 21 routes
.
India's first indigenous
hydrogen fuel cell-powered train
began operations on the Jind–Sonipat section in July 2026.
Geo Thermal
Geothermal energy offers a reliable renewable source that can complement variable sources such as solar and wind. Geothermal energy uses heat stored within the Earth to generate electricity or provide direct heat.
National Policy on Geothermal Energy (notified on 15 September 2025)
The policy provides a framework for the exploration, development and utilisation of geothermal resources.
The Geological Survey of India has estimated
India's geothermal potential at around 10,600 MW
, based on exploration across
381 hot springs
, with
42 geothermal manifestations
identified as promising areas.
The policy promotes technology partnerships, knowledge transfer and joint R&D. India has cooperation mechanisms with Australia, Iceland, Saudi Arabia and the United States for geothermal energy.
Five projects sanctioned during July–August 2025
, including a
pilot production plant, resource assessment projects and a solar–geothermal hybrid plant
. These aim to establish the
techno-economic viability
of geothermal applications.
Looking Ahead: Building India’s Energy Future
India is building an energy system powered increasingly by
clean, renewable sources
. Expanding solar, wind, hydro and bio-energy capacity is being supported by domestic manufacturing, energy storage and emerging technologies such as green hydrogen and geothermal energy.
As energy demand grows, renewable energy will support
reliable power, greater energy security and a cleaner future
. Continued policy support and technological progress will help build an energy system that is
sustainable, self-reliant and future-ready
.

title: NPPA Directs Strict Monitoring of Implementation of TMR on 137 Anti-Cancer Drugs
subtitle: State Drug Controllers to Submit Action Taken Report by 16 November
ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Pharmaceuticals
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                13 NOV 2026 12:35PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, has directed strict monitoring of the implementation of Trade Margin Rationalisation (TMR) on 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs, notified vide Gazette Order dated 17 October 2026, with revised prices effective from 9 November 2026.
The latest revised price lists, based on submissions received from companies up to 11 November 2026, are available on the
NPPA website and Pharma Sahi Daam app/portal
. All
manufacturers, retailers, dealers, stockists, hospitals and medical institutions
have been directed to comply with the revised prices and prominently display the updated price lists at their premises and websites.
State Drug Controllers to Ensure Compliance and Protect Patients' Interests :
State Drug Controllers (SDCs) have been directed to strictly monitor compliance by manufacturers, dealers, hospitals and medical institutions to ensure that the benefits of revised MRPs are passed on to patients. Any violation may attract overcharging proceedings under the provisions of
DPCO, 2013.
Complaints regarding overcharging, shortage or non-availability of medicines can be reported through the
Pharma Sahi Daam app/portal, NPPA
helpline (1800-111-255)
or email
(monitoring-nppa@gov.in.)
State Drug Controllers have been asked to submit their Action Taken Reports to NPPA by 16 November 2026.
